ITQAN:v2p364/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p364/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p364/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains عن ساق as the severity of the Hereafter; an anonymous line uses ساق for the intensity of war.
ITQAN:v2p364/r2.anchor: قال عن شدة الآخرة أما سمعت قول الشاعر ( قد قامت بنا الحرب على ساق )

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p420/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p420/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p420/r1.claim: The Hereafter challenge asks disbelievers to prove their claimed entitlement through scripture, oath, or guarantors, while assuring the Prophet that their delusion will be exposed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p420/r1.anchor: if they have any oath from God in this regard or if there are some people who have assured them of this, then they should present this evidence

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p438/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p438/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p438/r2.claim: Kashf sāq is a common Arabic idiom for a severe situation; Ḥātim Ṭā’ī’s battle couplet illustrates it with a warrior meeting the crisis head-on.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p438/r2.anchor: a common Arabic idiom to express the severity of a situation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p438/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p438/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p438/r3.claim: The idiom evokes upheaval forcing modest women to flee with garments raised, exposing shins and jewelry; a cited poem depicts elders forgetting their children and a woman’s shins exposed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p438/r3.anchor: chaste and decent ladies are forced to flee while raising their legwear, as a result of which, both their shins and the jewelry

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r4.claim: Some interpreters, relying on a report, take the phrase as God exposing His shin; Islahi rejects that reading in favor of the Arabic idiom for severity.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r5.speaker: Ibn ‘Abbās
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r5.claim: In a report transmitted by ʿIkrimah, Ibn ʿAbbās interprets it as Judgment Day, marked by harshness and brutality.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r5.anchor: A narrative from Ibn ‘Abbās (rta), reported by ‘Ikramah says that it refers to the Day of Judgement

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r6.speaker: Ibn Jarīr Tabarī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r6.claim: Tabarī records, on Ibn ʿAbbās’s authority, a poet’s opinion supporting the idiomatic reading of sāq.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r6.anchor: the opinion of a poet in support of this opinion

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r7.speaker: Mujāhid
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r7.claim: Mujāhid also adopts the interpretation that the phrase denotes a severe day.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310#2/r2.claim: Qatada interprets the uncovering of the shin as the severity of the event.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ يوم يكشف عن ساق ﴾ قال يكشف عن شدة الأمر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310#2/r3.claim: Ibn Masud interprets it literally as God's shin.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله تعالى ﴿ يوم يكشف عن ساق ﴾ قال يعني ساقه تبارك وتعالى

QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r13.claim: Uncovering the shin can signify the severity of Judgment Day; another exegetical view takes it as the shin of the Throne.
QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r13.anchor: عن ساق } : أي عن شدة يوم القيامة . ويقال في التفسير عن ساق العرش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p246/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p246/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p246/r4.claim: The majority and apparent view identifies the day of the ساق with the Resurrection; syntactically يوم can depend on فليأتوا, on an understood اذكر, or on an omitted clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p246/r4.anchor: والظاهر وقول الجمهور: أن هذا اليوم هو يوم القيامة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p246/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p246/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p246/r5.claim: He places the day in worldly life, at death or during illness and old age, since the Resurrection has no acts of worship or legal duties.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p246/r5.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: هذا اليوم هو في الدنيا لأنه قال: ويدعون إلى السجود، ويوم القيامة ليس فيه تعبد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p246/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p246/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p246/r6.claim: The invitation to prostrate is not a new legal command but a rebuke; their capacity is withheld so regret grows over neglecting the call when sound.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p246/r6.anchor: وأجيب بأن الدعاء إلى السجود ليس على سبيل التكليف، بل على سبيل التقريع والتخجيل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r1.claim: The phrase كشف عن ساق is a widespread Arabic metaphor for a crisis and its terrible severity, as shown by several poems about war and drought.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r1.anchor: محمول أيضا على الشدة في ذلك اليوم، وهو مجاز شائع في لسان العرب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r2.claim: He explains يوم يكشف عن ساق as a day that reveals overwhelming hardship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يوم يكشف عن شدة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r3.claim: He says the expression denotes hardship; Arabs use كشف عن ساق for girding oneself, including describing a year of drought.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r3.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: هذه كلمة تستعمل في الشدة، يقال: كشف عن ساقه إذا تشمر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r4.claim: The indefinite ساق signals an unknown, extraordinary calamity, likened to the unprecedented terror in 54:6.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r4.anchor: ونكر ساق للدلالة على أنه أمر مبهم في الشدة، خارج عن المألوف، كقوله تعالى: يوم يدع الداع إلى شيء نكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r5.claim: The call to prostrate is, in the apparent reading, a rebuke rather than a legal obligation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r5.anchor: ويدعون إلى السجود فلا يستطيعون: ظاهره أنهم يدعون، وتقدم أن ذلك على سبيل التوبيخ لا على سبيل التكليف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r6.claim: Another explanation is that seeing believers prostrate makes the others try to follow, but they cannot; a transmitted scene describes believers prostrating while hypocrites and disbelievers are physically prevented.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r6.anchor: وقيل: الداعي ما يرونه من سجود المؤمنين، فيريدون هم السجود فلا يستطيعونه، كما ورد في الحديث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r7.speaker: الجبائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r7.claim: The fact that they cannot prostrate in the afterlife does not prove, as al-Jubba'i argues, that they could do so in worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p247/r7.anchor: ونفي الاستطاعة للسجود في الآخرة لا يدل على أن لهم استطاعة في الدنيا، كما ذهب إليه الجبائي.

MAJAZ:v2p265/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p265/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p265/r6.claim: Yukshafu ʿan sāq is an idiom for war or a matter becoming severe; Qays ibn Zuhayr's verse illustrates it.
MAJAZ:v2p265/r6.anchor: «يوم يكشف عن ساق» (42) إذا اشتد الحرب والأمر قيل: قد كشف الأمر عن ساقه

MAJAZ:v2p265/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p265/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p265/r7.claim: Qays ibn Zuhayr ibn Judhaymah al-ʿAbsī uses the phrase for a crisis whose leg is bared.
MAJAZ:v2p265/r7.anchor:
قال قيس بن زهير بن جذيمة العبسى:
فإذ شمرت لك عن ساقها ... فويها ربيع ولا تسأم

QASHANI:68:16/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:68:16/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:68:16/r2.claim: The day the matter is uncovered is an indescribably severe ordeal, with bodily habits and pleasures removed and terrifying psychological forms and pains revealed.
QASHANI:68:16/r2.anchor: يوم يشتد الأمر وتتفاقم شدته بحيث لا يمكن وصفها بمفارقة المألوفات البدنية والملاذ الحسية

QASHANI:68:16/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:68:16/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:68:16/r3.claim: They are called by the realm of spirits to submit and receive divine lights, but cannot because dark dispositions and bodily veils have destroyed their original readiness.
QASHANI:68:16/r3.anchor: ويدعون } على لسان الملكوت للجنسية الأصلية والمناسبة الفطرية { إلى } سجود الإذعان والانقياد لقبول الأنوار الإلهية

RAZI-FULL:v30p82#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#3/r4.claim: After disproving their claim, the passage turns to the majesty of the Day of Resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#3/r4.anchor: شرح بعد ذلك عظمة يوم القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r1.claim: Yawm may be accusative as the time for the preceding challenge to bring partners, attached to an implied udhkur, or followed by an omitted event whose deletion heightens awe.
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r1.anchor: يوم منصوب بماذا ؟ فيه ثلاثة أوجه

RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r2.claim: The majority place the uncovering on the Day of Resurrection and explain the shin as a figure for hardship and distress.

RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r3.claim: Asked about the verse, Ibn ʿAbbās advised seeking Arabic poetry when Quranic meaning is unclear, since poetry is the Arabs’ register, and cited a line about war standing on a shin to mean distress.
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r3.anchor: روي أنه سئل ابن عباس عن هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r4.claim: The verse Ibn ʿAbbās quotes, “war stood on a shin,” uses sāq for severe distress.

RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r5.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r5.claim: Mujāhid transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that the phrase means the most severe hour of the Resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r5.anchor: وروى مجاهد عنه قال : هو أشد ساعة في القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r6.claim: An anonymous verse about a shin being bared likewise uses the phrase for a moment requiring resolve.

RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r7.claim: Another anonymous couplet, “she bared her shin and plain evil appeared,” uses the shin as a figure for a grave crisis.
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r7.anchor: كشفت لكم عن ساقها وبدا من الشر الصراح

RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r8.speaker: جرير
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r8.claim: Jarīr’s line about war baring its shin witnesses to sāq as a figure for war’s severity.
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r8.anchor: وقال جرير : ألا رب سام الطرف

RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r9.claim: An anonymous line about a red year baring its shin uses the expression for a year of hardship.
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r9.anchor: في سنة قد شمرت عن ساقها حمراء تبرى اللحم عن عراقها

RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r10.claim: An anonymous exhortation to tighten one’s resolve as war bares its shin likewise witnesses to the idiom of severity.
RAZI-FULL:v30p82#4/r10.anchor: قد شمرت عن ساقها فشدوا وجدت الحرب بكم فجدوا

RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba traces the idiom to people rolling up their clothes to work hard in a serious matter; hence uncovering the shin figuratively means distress.
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أصل هذا أن الرجل إذاوقع في أمر عظيم

RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r2.claim: Rāzī says the idiom’s use for hardship is metaphorical; since decisive proofs establish that God is not a body, the wording must be interpreted figuratively.
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r2.anchor: فإذا أقمنا الدلائل القاطعة على أنه تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r3.claim: The author of al-Kashshāf reads the phrase as a metaphor for an affair becoming severe, with no actual uncovering or shin, like calling a miser’s hand tied.
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r3.anchor: صاحب ( الكشاف ) أورد هذا التأويل في معرض آخر

RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r4.claim: Rāzī says metaphor without proof would license philosophers to turn gardens and rivers in 2:25 or bowing and prostration in 22:77 into mere figures, undermining revealed law.
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r4.anchor: إن جوزنا ذلك انفتحت أبواب تأويلات الفلاسفة

RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r5.claim: If the metaphor is allowed only after proof that the literal sense is impossible, Rāzī says this is the standard theologians’ method, not a special discovery of rhetorical science.
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r5.anchor: فهذا هو الذي لم يزل كل أحد من المتكلمين

RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الضرير
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r6.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḍarīr takes sāq as the basis or core of a matter, as a tree’s or person’s shin supports it; realities and fundamentals will appear at Resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r6.anchor: قول أبي سعيد الضرير : { يوم يكشف عن ساق }

RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r7.claim: Other explanations identify the shin as belonging to Hell, the Throne, or a mighty, awe-inspiring angel; the wording does not identify which.
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r7.anchor: القول الثالث : يوم يكشف عن ساق جهنم

RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r8.speaker: المشبهة
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r8.claim: Anthropomorphists take the shin to be God’s; a report attributed to Ibn Masʿūd from the Prophet says God reveals it after questioning the worshippers, believers prostrate, and hypocrites’ backs become rigid.
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r8.anchor: والقول الرابع : وهو اختيار المشبهة ، أنه ساق الله

RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r9.claim: Rāzī rejects a divine body: bodies are finite and originated, are subject to motion and rest, and are contingent; an indefinite shin also suits an immense hardship better than a known divine limb, while uncovering a shin would not identify God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r9.anchor: الدلائل دلت على أن كل جسم محدث

RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r10.claim: Abū Muslim places the event in worldly life, not Resurrection: perhaps a person’s final day, when prayer is called but belief no longer benefits, or infirmity through old age and illness; he compares 25:22 and 56:83.

RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r11.claim: Rāzī answers Abū Muslim’s objection that Resurrection has no legal obligations: the call to prostrate can be rebuke and humiliation rather than a legal duty.
RAZI-FULL:v30p83/r11.anchor: فجوابه أن ذلك لا يكون على سبيل التكليف

RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r1.claim: Reported readings use nūn or tāʾ in the verb, with active or passive construction and the Hour or the situation as subject; the sense is that the situation grows severe, by metaphor.

RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r2.claim: Another reading has ta with ḍamma and shin with kasra, from akshafa, meaning to enter into a state of uncovering; akshaf describes an upturned upper lip.

RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r3.claim: The call to prostrate in the Hereafter is not worship or legal obligation but rebuke for having abandoned prostration in worldly life.
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r3.anchor: لا يدعون إلى السجود تعبدا وتكليفا

RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r4.claim: At the call, God removes their ability to prostrate and blocks their capacity, heightening regret for neglecting the call when their limbs were sound.

RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r5.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r5.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī argues that specifying inability to the Hereafter proves disbelievers had the ability to believe in worldly life, contrary to those who deny such capacity without actual faith.
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r5.anchor: قال الجبائي : لما خصص عدم الاستطاعة

RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r6.claim: Rāzī replies that, on al-Jubbāʾī’s own view, God’s knowledge that a person will not believe is incompatible with that belief, so worldly capacity is absent too.
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r6.anchor: أن علم الله بأنه لا يؤمن مناف لوجود الإيمان والجمع بين المتنافيين محال

STUDYQURAN:68:42/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r1.claim: The shank being laid bare is an idiom for a very serious and severe situation.
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r1.anchor: The shank is laid bare is an idiomatic expression indicating something very serious and severe

STUDYQURAN:68:42/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r2.claim: In strenuous effort or battle, Arabs rolled up their garments to expose the shank; the idiom “war broke out upon the shank” means war began vehemently.
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r2.anchor: he begins by rolling up his garment in such a fashion that his shank is exposed

STUDYQURAN:68:42/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r3.claim: The Arabic idiom “war broke out upon the shank” means that war broke out with vehemence.
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r3.anchor: “The war broke out upon the shank,” meaning “The war broke out with vehemence”

STUDYQURAN:68:42/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r4.claim: Some exegetes say God exposes His own Shank to signal the beginning of the Judgment process.
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r4.anchor: Some exegetes say that in this verse it is God Who exposes His own Shank to signal the beginning of the judgment process

STUDYQURAN:68:42/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r5.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r5.claim: A variant reading, “We lay bare the shank,” makes God the one who exposes it.
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r5.anchor: meaning God (Q). Others say the shank is laid bare

STUDYQURAN:68:42/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r6.claim: Others understand the shank being laid bare as the unveiling of secrets.
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r6.anchor: Others say the shank is laid bare refers to the secrets that will be unveiled.

STUDYQURAN:68:42/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r7.speaker: ḥadīth
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r7.claim: A report says God will expose His Shank; sincere believers will prostrate, while those who performed prayer for show will be unable, their backs stiffened like a plate.
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r7.anchor: a ḥadīth states, “God will lay bare His Shank and then the believers, men and women, will prostrate before Him

STUDYQURAN:68:42/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r8.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r8.claim: A third reading, “It lays bared the shank,” means the Resurrection exposes great severities.
STUDYQURAN:68:42/r8.anchor: meaning that the Resurrection exposes great severities (Q)

STUDYQURAN:68:43/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:43/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:43/r2.claim: One interpretation takes the prostration in both verses as prostration for prayer in worldly life.
STUDYQURAN:68:43/r2.anchor: references to prostrating for prayer in this world

STUDYQURAN:68:43/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:43/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:43/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes verse 42 as prostration on Judgment Day and verse 43 as the worldly call to prayer that the disbelievers ignored; their later inability follows from refusing to prostrate when sound.
STUDYQURAN:68:43/r3.anchor: v. 42 as a reference to prostration on the Day of Judgment and v. 43 as a reference to those who did not heed the call to prostration, meaning to prayer, in this world

TAB-FULL:v23p187/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r1.claim: Al-Tabari frames the phrase, following a group of early exegetes, as the disclosure of a severe affair.
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {يوم يكشف عن ساق} [القلم: 42] قال: هو يوم حرب وشدة

TAB-FULL:v23p187/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ikrima, calls it a day of war and hardship.
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {يوم يكشف عن ساق} [القلم: 42] قال: هو يوم حرب وشدة

TAB-FULL:v23p187/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses it as a great affair and cites an Arabic battle expression and poetic line as evidence for the idiom of hardship.
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {يوم يكشف عن ساق} [القلم: 42]

TAB-FULL:v23p187/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r4.claim: Ibrahim reports that every believer will prostrate, while the disbeliever's back hardens into a single bone.
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r4.anchor: عن مغيرة، عن إبراهيم، {يوم يكشف عن ساق} [القلم: 42] ولا يبقى مؤمن إلا سجد، ويقسو ظهر الكافر

TAB-FULL:v23p187/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the affair is uncovered, deeds become apparent, and this unveiling marks entry into the afterlife.
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} [القلم: 42] يقول: حين يكشف الأمر، وتبدو الأعمال

TAB-FULL:v23p187/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r6.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas calls it the terrifying, severe affair of the Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} [القلم: 42] هو الأمر الشديد المفظع من الهول يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v23p187/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r7.claim: Mujahid explains the phrase as the severity and gravity of the affair.
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} [القلم: 42] قال: شدة الأمر وجده

TAB-FULL:v23p187/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas describes it as the first hour of the Resurrection; another wording in the report calls it the most severe hour.
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هي أول ساعة تكون في يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v23p187/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r9.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr glosses it as the severity of the affair.
TAB-FULL:v23p187/r9.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: عن شدة الأمر

TAB-FULL:v23p189/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r1.claim: Qatada calls the disclosure a tremendous, frightening event and a day when the affair becomes severe.
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} [القلم: 42] قال: عن أمر فظيع جليل

TAB-FULL:v23p189/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas cites the pre-Islamic idiom that war girds up its shank, explaining it as the afterlife's arrival and the world's passing.
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r2.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يقول: كان أهل الجاهلية يقولون: شمرت الحرب عن ساق، يعني إقبال الآخرة وذهاب الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v23p189/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r3.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r3.claim: Abdullah reports that people are questioned about whom they worship; when the shank is disclosed, believers prostrate while hypocrites' backs become flat and rigid.
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: يتمثل الله للخلق يوم القيامة حتى يمر المسلمون، قال: فيقول: من تعبدون؟

TAB-FULL:v23p189/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r4.claim: Ibn Mas'ud describes forty years of standing, idol worshippers being led to Hell, and believers prostrating while hypocrites cannot; believers then enter Paradise and receive its rewards.
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، قال: ينادي مناد يوم القيامة: أليس عدلا من ربكم الذي خلقكم

TAB-FULL:v23p191/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p191/r1.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v23p191/r1.claim: Abdullah tells Umar that after forty years of standing, each people follows its objects of worship to Hell; Muslims prostrate when the Lord appears, but hypocrites cannot and are sent to Hell, while believers enter Paradise and are rewarded.
TAB-FULL:v23p191/r1.anchor: عن قيس بن سكن، قال: حدث عبد الله

TAB-FULL:v23p191/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p191/r2.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v23p191/r2.claim: A second account from Abdullah to Umar repeats the gathering, idol-following and return to God, where true worshippers prostrate and hypocrites' backs stiffen before they are taken to Hell.
TAB-FULL:v23p191/r2.anchor: قال عبد الله وهو يحدث عمر

TAB-FULL:v23p194/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p194/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p194/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits a Prophetic report: worshippers prostrate at the disclosure, hypocrites' backs fuse, and survivors cross the bridge at different speeds according to their light; al-Tabari abridges a longer report.
TAB-FULL:v23p194/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " حتى إن أحدهم ليلتف فيكشف عن ساق، فيقعون سجودا

TAB-FULL:v23p194/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p194/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p194/r2.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that idol worshippers, Jews and Christians follow what they worship to Hell; those left recognize God at the disclosure and prostrate, while hypocrites who did not prostrate sincerely cannot.
TAB-FULL:v23p194/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إذا كان يوم القيامة نادى مناد: ألا لتلحق كل أمة بما كانت تعبد

TAB-FULL:v23p195/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p195/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p195/r1.claim: A second transmission from Abu Sa'id repeats that each group follows what it worshipped; the remaining people wait for their Lord, whose coming is related to the preceding account.
TAB-FULL:v23p195/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " ينادي مناديه فيقول: ليلحق كل قوم بما كانوا يعبدون

TAB-FULL:v23p195/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p195/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p195/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that after settling wrongs, God sends angels resembling Uzayr and Jesus and presents false gods; believers affirm only God, recognize Him by a sign and prostrate, while hypocrites fall backward with rigid spines.
TAB-FULL:v23p195/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " يأخذ الله للمظلوم من الظالم حتى إذا لم يبق تبعة لأحد عند أحد

TAB-FULL:v23p196/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p196/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p196/r1.claim: Abu Musa, through Abu Burda, reports the Prophet saying that the disclosure is a great light before which they prostrate.
TAB-FULL:v23p196/r1.anchor: عن أبي بردة بن أبي موسى، عن أبيه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} [القلم: 42] قال: «عن نور عظيم يخرون له سجدا»

TAB-FULL:v23p196/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p196/r2.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v23p196/r2.claim: Al-Rabi' interprets the disclosure as the lifting of a veil.
TAB-FULL:v23p196/r2.anchor: عن أبي جعفر، عن الربيع، في قول الله {يوم يكشف عن ساق} [القلم: 42] قال: يكشف عن الغطاء

TAB-FULL:v23p196/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p196/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p196/r3.claim: Ikrima calls it a day of distress and hardship.
TAB-FULL:v23p196/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} [القلم: 42] قال: هو يوم كرب وشدة

TAB-FULL:v23p196/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p196/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p196/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as the Resurrection's disclosure of extreme hardship, citing the Arabic idiom for an affair entering difficulty.
TAB-FULL:v23p196/r4.anchor: وذكر عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ ذلك: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} [القلم: 42] بمعنى تكشف القيامة عن شدة شديدة، والعرب تقول

TAB-FULL:v23p196/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p196/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p196/r5.claim: Al-Tabari cites an anonymous poetic line in which a woman's shank is uncovered and clear evil appears, as evidence for the idiom of hardship.
TAB-FULL:v23p196/r5.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر: [البحر الكامل] كشفت لهم عن ساقها … وبدا من الشر الصراح

TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r7.claim: Qatada transmits a Prophetic report that believers will be allowed to prostrate at the Resurrection; hypocrites cannot, and believers' prostration rebukes and humiliates them.
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r7.anchor: ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول: «يؤذن للمؤمنين يوم القيامة في السجود، فيسجد المؤمنون

TAB-FULL:v1p56/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p56/r1.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
TAB-FULL:v1p56/r1.claim: Abū Qilābah reports that teachers’ different readings led students to accuse one another of error or unbelief; Uthman called for a standard codex, saying distant regions differed even more.
TAB-FULL:v1p56/r1.anchor: فبلغ ذلك عثمان، فقام خطيبا، فقال: أنتم عندي تختلفون فيه وتلحنون

TAB-FULL:v1p56/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p56/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v1p56/r2.claim: Anas says disputed verses were left unwritten until someone who had learned them from the Prophet arrived; after completing the codex, Uthman sent copies to the provinces and ordered other copies erased.
TAB-FULL:v1p56/r2.anchor: فحدثني أنس بن مالك، قال: كنت فيمن يملى عليهم، قال: فربما اختلفوا في الآية

TAB-FULL:v1p56/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p56/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v1p56/r3.claim: Anas reports that disagreements between Syrian and Iraqi troops at Azerbaijan and Armenia nearly caused strife; Hudhayfah warned Uthman of divisions like those among Jews and Christians, so Uthman copied Hafsah’s sheets and dispatched codices.
TAB-FULL:v1p56/r3.anchor: أنس بن مالك الأنصاري أنه اجتمع في غزوة أذربيجان وأرمينية أهل الشام وأهل العراق

TAB-FULL:v1p56/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p56/r4.speaker: الزهري
TAB-FULL:v1p56/r4.claim: Al-Zuhrī says the Prophet died before the Qur’an was compiled as a codex; it remained on palm stalks and fronds.
TAB-FULL:v1p56/r4.anchor: عن الزهري، قال: «قبض النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، ولم يكن القرآن جمع، وإنما كان في الكرانيف والعسب»

TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r1.claim: Yawm is an adverb of time attached to an omitted imperative such as “remember.”
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r1.anchor: يوم ظرف متعلق بمحذوف كاذكر ونحوه

TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r2.claim: Uncovering the shin is a metaphor for an extreme crisis, since people roll up their sleeves when hard pressed to work or flee.
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r2.anchor: والكشف عن الساق تمثيل في اشتداد الأمر اشتدادا بالغا لما أنهم كانوا يشمرون عن سوقهم إذا اشتد الأمر

TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r3.speaker: الكشاف
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r3.claim: Al-Kashshāf reads the phrase as the intensification of crisis, with no literal uncovering or shin, like describing a miser’s hand as shackled though no hand or shackle is meant.
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r3.anchor: قال في الكشاف فمعنى { يوم يكشف عن ساق } في معنى

TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r4.claim: These five verses interrupt the discussion because the alleged partners were supposed to secure happiness after resurrection; there are no partners or intercession, and afterlife felicity comes from worldly submission to God’s unity in lordship.
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r4.anchor: والآية وما بعدها إلى تمام خمس آيات اعتراض وقع في البين بمناسبة ذكر شركائهم الذين يزعمون أنهم سيسعدونهم لو كان هناك بعث وحساب

TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r5.claim: The deniers cannot prostrate in the afterlife because arrogance became an established trait in their hidden selves; on that day inner realities are exposed.
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r5.anchor: فلا يستطيعون لاستقرار ملكة الاستكبار في سرائرهم واليوم تبلى السرائر

BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r4.claim: Yawm is governed by an omitted udhkur, and ʿan sāq stands in the passive as the deputy subject of yukshafu.
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r4.anchor: يوم منصوب باذكر المقدر وعن ساق قائم مقام الفاعل ليكشف

BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r5.claim: The phrase means the Day of Resurrection, when distress becomes severe; it is an idiom, like saying a miser's hand is tied, with no literal hand-binding or uncovering of a shin.
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r5.anchor: وكشف الساق مثل في ذلك ولا كشف ولا ساق ثمة كما تقول للأقطع الشحيح

BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r6.claim: The composite image likens the gathering's afflicted people to modest women forced to hike their skirts to flee a terrifying emergency; the simile is in the syntactic configuration, not the individual words.
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r6.anchor: من غير تصرف في مفردات التركيب بل التصرف إنما هو في الهيئة التركيبية

BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r7.speaker: الفناري
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r7.claim: Al-Fanārī says the uncovered shin represents an immense eschatological ordeal; Arabs say war has uncovered its shin when its severity is great, and the shins merging signal horrors piled together.
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r7.anchor: قال المولى الفناري في تفسير الفاتحة فالساق التي كشفت لهم عبارة عن أمر عظيم

BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r8.claim: Another view takes sāq as the foundation that sustains a thing, like a tree or human leg, so unveiling it means the roots and realities of affairs become manifest.
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r8.anchor: وقيل ساق الشيء أصله الذي به قوامه كساق الشجر وساق الإنسان

BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r9.claim: On the severe-event interpretation, the indefinite form magnifies terror; on the foundational-reality interpretation, it conveys exaltation.
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r9.anchor: وتنكيره على الوجه الأول للتهويل لأن يوم القيامة يوم يقع فيه أمر فظيع

BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r10.claim: The people summoned are unbelievers and hypocrites, called to prostrate as rebuke for having abandoned it in worldly life and to deepen their regret.
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r10.anchor: توبيخا وتعنيفاف على تركهم إياه في الدنيا وتحسيرا لهم على تفريطهم

BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r11.claim: The call is not a renewed obligation to worship, since the Resurrection is not a time of legal duty or ritual worship.
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r11.anchor: لأن يوم القيامة لا يكون فيه تعيد ولا تكليف وسيأتي غير هذا

BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r12.claim: Their inability results from losing the real capacity, means, and bodily instruments needed to prostrate; the verse implies they do attempt it but cannot succeed.
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r12.anchor: لزوال القدرة الحقيقية عليه وسلامة الأسباب والآلات وفيه دلالة على أنهم يقصدون السجود

BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r13.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says their backs become a single vertebra, unable to bend when rising or bowing, so they remain standing and their regret grows; a hadith likewise says their backs remain one solid segment.
BURSEVI:v10p91#3/r13.anchor: ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه تعقم أصلابهم أي ترد عظاما بلا مفاصل لا تنثني

BURSEVI:v10p92/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p92/r1.speaker: أبو موسى
BURSEVI:v10p92/r1.claim: Abū Mūsā reports the Prophet's account: communities follow what they worshipped; the monotheists recognize God by His uniqueness, see Him when the veil is lifted, and prostrate, while others with rigid backs cannot; each believer is given a Jew or Christian in the Fire in his place.
BURSEVI:v10p92/r1.anchor: عن أبي بردة عن أبي موسى رضي الله عنه قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بقول إذا كان يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v10p92/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p92/r2.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
BURSEVI:v10p92/r2.claim: When Abū Bardah relayed the report, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz swore that it came from his father and said he had heard no report from the monotheists he liked more.
BURSEVI:v10p92/r2.anchor: والله الذي لا إله إلا هو أحدثك أبوك بهذا الحديث فحلفت له بثلاث إيمان فقال

BURSEVI:v10p92/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p92/r3.speaker: الفناري
BURSEVI:v10p92/r3.claim: Al-Fanārī describes the community remaining with its hypocrites, who reject an initial manifestation and recognize God only when He appears in the familiar form marked by their sign; true worshippers prostrate, while those who prostrated in ostentation are made to fall backward.
BURSEVI:v10p92/r3.anchor: وفي تفسير الفاتحة للفناري رحمه الله يتجلى الحق في ذلك اليوم فيقول لتتبع كل أمة ما كانت عبد

BURSEVI:v10p92/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p92/r4.speaker: الفناري
BURSEVI:v10p92/r4.claim: Al-Fanārī says people on the Heights with equal scales are called to prostrate; this is the remaining duty in the Hereafter, and their prostration tips their good deeds so they enter Paradise.
BURSEVI:v10p92/r4.anchor: وقال أيضا يكون عى الأعراف من تساوت كفتا ميزانه فهم ينظرون إلى النار

BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r1.speaker: الأشاعرة
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r1.claim: On the question of assigning a task that cannot be fulfilled, Ashʿarites permit it and Muʿtazilites forbid it; no one permits assigning what is intrinsically irrational, such as annihilating the eternal.
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r1.anchor: وقد أجاز الأشاعرة التكليف به ومنعه المعتزلة وإما المحال العقلي وهو الممتنع لذاته

TABRISI:68:39-42/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:39-42/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:39-42/r6.claim: The phrase means the day when a terrible matter and the day's horrors become manifest.
TABRISI:68:39-42/r6.anchor: وقيل: معناه يوم يبدو عن الأمر الشديد الفظيع عن ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة

TABRISI:68:39-42/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:39-42/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:68:39-42/r7.claim: When asked about the phrase, Ibn Abbas said obscure Qur'anic expressions should be sought in Arabic poetry, the Arabs' record; he cited a line saying war rose upon a shin to express distress.
TABRISI:68:39-42/r7.anchor: سأل ابن عباس عن قوله { يوم يكشف عن ساق } فقال: إذا خفي عليكم شيء

TABRISI:68:39-42/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:39-42/r8.speaker: القتيبي
TABRISI:68:39-42/r8.claim: Al-Qutaybi explains the idiom from a person exposing his shin when a grave task demands exertion; Duraid ibn al-Simma's verse illustrates it.
TABRISI:68:39-42/r8.anchor: وقال القتيبي: أصل هذا أن الرجل إذا وقع في أمر عظيم يحتاج إلى الجد فيه يشمر عن ساقه

TABRISI:68:42-45/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:42-45/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:42-45/r1.claim: The phrase means the day the affair becomes severe, like a situation requiring someone to roll up his clothes and expose a shin.
TABRISI:68:42-45/r1.anchor: فتأويل الآية يوم يشتد الأمر كما يشتد ما يحتاج فيه إلى أن يكشف عن ساق

TABRISI:68:42-45/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:42-45/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:42-45/r2.claim: They are told to prostrate as a rebuke, but cannot do so.
TABRISI:68:42-45/r2.anchor: أي يقال لهم على وجه التوبيخ اسجدوا

TABRISI:68:42-45/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:42-45/r3.speaker: قول آخر
TABRISI:68:42-45/r3.claim: Alternatively, the day's difficulty drives them to prostrate though it can no longer benefit them, as people instinctively prostrate when frightened in worldly life.
TABRISI:68:42-45/r3.anchor: وقيل: معناه أن شدة الأمر وصعوبة ذلك اليوم تدعوهم إلى السجود وإن كانوا لا ينتفعون به

TABRISI:68:42-45/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:42-45/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:42-45/r12.claim: A report says the backs of hypocrites become like spits or skewers.
TABRISI:68:42-45/r12.anchor: وفي الخبر أنه تصير ظهور المنافقين كالسفافيد

THALABI:v10p18#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p18#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p18#2/r1.claim: The unveiling of the shin denotes a dreadful, severe affair: the arrival of the Hereafter and the end of worldly life.
THALABI:v10p18#2/r1.anchor: أي عن أمر شديد فظيع، وهو إقبال الآخرة.

THALABI:v10p18#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p18#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p18#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the verb in the feminine, making the Resurrection uncover its shin.
THALABI:v10p18#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس بتاء مفتوحة، أي يكشف القيامة عن ساقها.

THALABI:v10p18#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p18#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p18#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan also reads the verb in the feminine, while retaining the sense of a dreadful, severe affair.
THALABI:v10p18#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بتاء مضمومة عن ساق أي عن أمر شديد فظيع،

THALABI:v10p18#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p18#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p18#2/r4.claim: The phrase is an Arabic metaphor for a crisis requiring strenuous effort; an affair can be said to uncover its shin although it has no leg.

THALABI:v10p18#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p18#2/r5.speaker: دريد بن الصمة
THALABI:v10p18#2/r5.claim: Duraid ibn al-Simma's elegy describes a man with half his shin exposed, illustrating the literal image behind the expression.
THALABI:v10p18#2/r5.anchor: قال دريد بن الصمة يرثي رجلا: كميش الإزار خارج نصف ساقه

THALABI:v10p18#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p18#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p18#2/r6.claim: Arabic also uses uncovering the shin for the emergence of a severe affair; war poems call war a woman who uncovers her shin.
THALABI:v10p18#2/r6.anchor: ويقال للأمر إذا اشتد وتفاقم وظهر وزالت عماه: كشف عن ساقه،

THALABI:v10p18#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p18#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p18#2/r7.claim: A poem attributed to Ibn Abbas urges patience in lasting hardship and says war has risen on its shin.
THALABI:v10p18#2/r7.anchor: وأنشد ابن عباس: اصبر عناق أنه شر باق

THALABI:v10p18#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p18#2/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v10p18#2/r8.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr explains the verse as the severity of the affair.
THALABI:v10p18#2/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير: يوم يكشف عن ساق قال: عن شدة الأمر.

THALABI:v10p18#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p18#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p18#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies it as the most severe hour on the Day of Resurrection.
THALABI:v10p18#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هي أشد ساعة في يوم القيامة.

THALABI:v10p19/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p19/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p19/r1.claim: Abu Musa reports that the unveiling is a great light before which people fall in prostration.
THALABI:v10p19/r1.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: يوم يكشف عن ساق قال: «نور عظيم يخرون له سجدا»

THALABI:v10p19/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p19/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p19/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the comparison of seeing God to the unobscured sun and full moon; at judgment false gods lead their worshippers away, while remaining believers recognize God at the sign of the shin and prostrate, unlike hypocrites.
THALABI:v10p19/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قلنا: يا رسول الله هل نرى ربنا يوم القيامة؟

THALABI:v10p19/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p19/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p19/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that after justice is settled, each community is called to its deity; Jews and Christians follow angelic likenesses of Ezra and Jesus, who lead them to the Fire, as in 21:98.
THALABI:v10p19/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يأخذ الله تعالى للمظلوم من الظالم، حتى لا يبقى مظلمة

THALABI:v10p21/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p21/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
THALABI:v10p21/r1.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri reports that nations follow their objects of worship toward the Fire; the remaining worshippers of God reject a false claim, recognize God when the shin is uncovered, and prostrate, while hypocrites cannot.
THALABI:v10p21/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إذا كان يوم القيامة نادى مناد

THALABI:v10p21#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p21#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله
THALABI:v10p21#2/r1.claim: A report transmitted by al-Tabari from Abdullah, who was with Umar, says people stand barefoot and naked for forty years; at the divine sign true worshippers prostrate, hypocrites cannot, and the former enter Paradise while the latter enter the Fire.
THALABI:v10p21#2/r1.anchor: عن المنهال عن قيس بن بكر، قال: حدثني عبد الله وهو عند عمر قال: إذا كان يوم القيامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r1.claim: The day phrase attaches to the preceding challenge: if their claimed partners are real, let them bring them on Judgment Day to benefit and intercede, but those claims fail.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r1.anchor: يقول الله: {إن كانوا صادقين} في أنها شركاء فليأتوا بها يوم القيامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r2.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r2.claim: ʿIkrima reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that “uncovering the shin” means severe distress, citing an Arabic line about war rising on a leg.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r2.anchor: روى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: عن شدة. ألم تسمع إلى قول الشاعر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says unclear Qurʾānic language should be sought in poetry, the Arabs’ record; he calls the verse a day of distress and hardship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r3.anchor: وسئل ابن عباس عن هذه الآية فقال: إذا خفي عليكم شيء من القرآن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r4.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r4.claim: ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn ʿAbbās explains it as hardship in the afterlife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r4.anchor: وروى عطاء عنه قال: يريد شدة في الآخرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r5.speaker: إبراهيم عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r5.claim: Ibrāhīm from Ibn ʿAbbās explains it as the severity of the event.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r5.anchor: وروى إبراهيم عنه أيضا: عن شدة الأمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r6.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās calls it the disclosure of a tremendous matter.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r6.anchor: قال (¬4): وقال ابن عباس يكشف عن أمر عظيم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r7.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r7.claim: Mujāhid reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that it is the most severe hour of the Resurrection; Saʿīd b. Jubayr, Mujāhid, and Qatāda likewise call it severe distress and great affliction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r7.anchor: وروى مجاهد عنه قال: هو أشد ساعة في القيامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says Arabs use “the matter uncovered its shin” for an intensifying crisis or war, citing Qays b. Zuhayr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r8.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: إذا اشتد الأمر والحرب قيل: قد كشف الأمر عن ساقه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r9.speaker: الفراء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that it is the Resurrection and Hour because of their severity, and cites an Arab poem.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r9.anchor: وروى الفراء بإسناده (¬5) عن ابن عباس (¬6) أنه قال: يريد يوم القيامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r10.claim: Abū Isḥāq interprets it as the revelation of a severe crisis and cites a poem about war’s shin being bared.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r10.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: معنى {يكشف عن ساق} كشف عن الأمر الشديد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r11.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r11.claim: Ibn Qutayba derives the idiom from a person in a great task pulling up his garment to work; exposing the shin became a metaphor for distress, supported by Arabic verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p111/r11.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: أصل هذا أن الرجل إذا وقع (¬4) في أمر عظيم يحتاج إلى معاناته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r1.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r1.claim: Another explanation paraphrases the verse as the day matters become as severe as a task requiring the shin to be uncovered; the expression became a proverb for hardship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r1.anchor: وزاد غيره بيانا فقال: تأويل الآية: يوم يشتد الأمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r2.claim: Muqātil says unbelievers’ spines will be fused into one bone like cattle horns because they did not prostrate to God in worldly life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: وذلك أنه تدمج أصلاب الكفار يومئذ فيكون عظما واحدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r3.speaker: جميع المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r3.claim: All exegetes say creatures prostrate once, but unbelievers and hypocrites then cannot prostrate because their backs have stiffened.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r3.anchor: وهذا قول جميع المفسرين (¬2). قالوا: إذا كان ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says believers fall prostrate, while hypocrites’ backs become board-like, as if containing spits or skewers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p114/r4.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: وأما المؤمنون فيخرون سجدا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:35-43/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:35-43/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:35-43/r8.claim: The “uncovering of a shin” means the onset of a severe affair, namely the Day of Resurrection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:35-43/r8.anchor: { يوم يكشف عن ساق } عن شدة من الأمر، وهو يوم القيامة.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:35-43/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:35-43/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:35-43/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this is the most severe hour of the Resurrection; “uncovering the shin” thus expresses the severity of the affair.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:35-43/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه: أشد ساعة في القيامة، فصار كشف الساق عبارة عن شدة الأمر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:35-43/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:35-43/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:35-43/r10.claim: The unbelievers and hypocrites cannot prostrate: their backs become a single plate, and when they try they fall backward.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:35-43/r10.anchor: { ويدعون إلى السجود } أي: الكافرون والمنافقون { فلا يستطيعون } يصير ظهرهم طبقا واحدا كلما أراد أن يسجد واحد منهم خر على قفاه.

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r4.claim: Saq literally means the shin from ankle toward calf, and by extension the basis or trunk of something; here it is indefinite and not annexed to anything.
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r4.anchor: lügatta mâlum ki topuktan baldıra doğru bacağın incik yeridir

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r5.claim: Abu Sa'id reports the Prophet: when the Lord unveils His shin, believers prostrate; those who prostrated ostentatiously in worldly life try, but their backs stiffen into one piece.
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r5.anchor: Buhârî, Müslim, Nesâî, İbn Münzir ve İbn Merdûye, Ebû Sa‘îd radıyallahu anh’tan şöyle bir hadîs rivayet etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r6.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports the Prophet: after each person is sent to follow the worldly deity they worshipped, Muslims recognize their Lord by the unveiling of the shin and prostrate, while hypocrites cannot bend their backs.
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r6.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd’dan, Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den bir hadis rivayet etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r7.speaker: Dârekutnî ve Hâkim
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r7.claim: Al-Daraqutni and al-Hakim grade the Ibn Mas'ud narration sound.

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r8.claim: The hadiths are ambiguous reports whose modality God will reveal in events at their appointed time; the unveiling signifies truth appearing from the unseen with terrible force, bringing mercy to truth's adherents and wrath to falsehood's.
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r8.anchor: hadislerde keyfiyeti ihâta olunamayacak müteşabih bir mâna vardır ki Allah teâlâ

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r9.claim: The image is a divine sign of truth's manifestation that strips people's veils of heedlessness and displays God's judgment; its actual manner cannot now be specified.
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r9.anchor: insanlardan gaflet perdelerini sıyıracak bir şiddet ve dehşetle hükm-i Hakk’ın ehl-i Hakk’a rahmet

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r10.claim: Elmalılı says the verse contains a symbolic sign like the letter nun.
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r10.anchor: Bu itibar ile burada da ن gibi bir remiz vardır

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r11.claim: Some seekers of ambiguous texts corporealize God against 42:11, while certain esoteric Sufis likewise insist on a literal visual manifestation; Elmalılı rejects such literalizing approaches.
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r11.anchor: koşan birtakım kimseler bunlardan tecsim ve teşbih

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r12.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r12.claim: The Kashshaf glosses uncovering the shin and baring calves as idioms for an affair's severity and calamity's difficulty, originating in people fleeing in terror with garments raised.
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r12.anchor: tâbirleri emrin şiddetinde ve musibetin su‘ûbetinde meseldir

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says obscure Qur'anic language should be investigated in poetry, the Arabs' register; the quoted line interprets the image as war at full severity.
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r13.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan bu âyetin tefsîri sorulduğunda demiştir ki

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the saq as hardship and severity, citing an Arabic verse about war standing on a shin.

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r15.speaker: مجاهِد
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r15.claim: Mujahid says this is the most severe hour of the Day of Resurrection.
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r15.anchor: Mücâhid de ondan bugün kıyametin en şiddetli saati olduğunu rivayet eylemiştir

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r16.claim: The cited Arabic poetry establishes that saq can figuratively mean severity; since definitive proofs rule out assigning a literal shin to God, the figurative sense is necessary.
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r16.anchor: Allah teâlâ’ya hakikat mânasıyla sâk isnâdı delâil-i kat‘iyye ile muhâl olduğundan mecaz ta‘ayyün eder

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r17.speaker: أبو سعيد الضرير
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r17.claim: Al-Razi reports Abu Sa'id al-Darir's view that saq is a thing's sustaining basis; unveiling it means the affair's core and the realities of things will emerge on Judgment Day.

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r18.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r18.claim: Al-Razi records a third proposal: the shin belongs to Hell, the Throne, or a majestic angel, though the verse names no possessor.
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r18.anchor: Üçüncü kavil, Cehennemin sâkı yahut Arş’ın sâkı yahut mehîb bir meleğin sâkı demektir

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r19.speaker: Müşebbihe
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r19.claim: Al-Razi reports that the Mushabbiha identify it as God's shin, but rejects corporeal attribution and reading related Ibn Mas'ud reports bodily; the verse's noun is indefinite.
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r19.anchor: Dördüncü kavil, Müşebbihe’nin ihtiyârıdır ki Allah’ın sâkı demişlerdir.

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r20.speaker: حاتم
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r20.claim: Hatem's line depicts reciprocal biting in war and war baring its calves, illustrating the idiom of extreme hardship.

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r1.speaker: ابن رقيات
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r1.claim: Ibn Rukayyat's poem says terror distracts an elder from his sons and makes a sheltered, modest young woman expose her calves, supporting the severity idiom.

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r2.claim: The phrase means God's command grows severe and the affair intensifies, not that a shin literally exists or is uncovered; describing a miser as hand-bound similarly conveys miserliness without a literal hand or bond.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r2.anchor: Yoksa ne sâk vardır ne de keşif

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r3.claim: Elmalılı rejects the corporeal reading of the Ibn Mas'ud hadith, explaining it as the intensification of God's command and the Great Terror of 21:103.

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r4.claim: The majority identifies this day as the Day of Resurrection.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r4.anchor: Birincisi, cumhûrun kavli: bugün kıyamet günüdür

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r5.claim: Abu Muslim says the day is in worldly life, since the verse describes people being called to prostrate and there is no worship or legal obligation at Resurrection.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r5.anchor: İkincisi de Ebû Müslim’in kavlidir ki bugün kıyamet günü değil, dünyadadır.

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r6.claim: Abu Muslim proposes either a person's last day, when angels appear without glad tidings and a late conversion no longer helps, or an illness, old age, or incapacity that prevents prostration despite earlier soundness.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r6.anchor: Ebû Müslim’in kavlidir ki bugün kıyamet günü değil, dünyadadır

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r7.claim: Elmalılı allows Abu Muslim's worldly reading but rejects his claim that Resurrection is impossible: the call there is reproach and condemnation, not a legal command; their imposed inability increases regret for neglecting prostration while sound.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r7.anchor: âyetin lafzını Ebû Müslim’in dediğine haml mümkin

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r8.speaker: أبو حيان
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan explains unveiling the shin as an idiom for affairs becoming severe; his citation treats the metaphor as common in Arabic.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r8.anchor: ‘Keşf-i sâk’ emrin şiddetinden ve gittikçe büyümesinden kinayedir

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r9.speaker: مجاهِد
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r9.claim: Mujahid identifies the severity as the most dreadful first hour of Resurrection.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r9.anchor: Mücâhid şöyle demiştir: Bu şiddet kıyametin ilk saatidir ve en fecî‘idir

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r10.speaker: راجز
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r10.claim: An anonymous rajiz describes a red drought year as exposing its shin and stripping meat from bones, another example of the severity idiom.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r10.anchor: beytinden başka râciz demiştir ki: عَجِبْتُ مِنْ نَفْسِي

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r11.speaker: راجز
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r11.claim: Another rajiz says war has bared its calves and grown serious, so the fighters must buckle down.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r11.anchor: Diğer bir râciz: قَدْ شَ َّمرَتْ عَنْ سَاقِهَا

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r12.speaker: راجز
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r12.claim: A further rajiz uses the idiom that war stands on a shin, exhorting steadfastness amid battle.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r12.anchor: Bir diğeri: صبرا امام آن شر ب اق

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r13.speaker: شاعر
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r13.claim: An unnamed poet says war revealed its shin and ruin appeared, extending the same hardship imagery.

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as a day when a severe ordeal is uncovered.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r14.anchor: İbn Abbas demiştir ki: يـَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ شِ َّدةٍ

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r15.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r15.claim: Abu Ubayda says saq is used for severity and kashafa an saqihi means gathering up one's garment; Arabs call a drought year one that has bared its shin.

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r16.speaker: Zemahşerî
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r16.claim: Zamakhshari says the indefinite saq points to an unfamiliar, extreme ordeal, like the unknown calamity named in 54:6.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r16.anchor: Zemahşerî’nin dediği gibi şiddette me’luftan hâriç bir emr-i mübheme

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r1.claim: Possessive attribution to God does not make a term such as 'shin' a divine part; each relation is determined by its terms, since God is indivisible.

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r2.claim: 'Rolling up the shin' can mean preparing, gathering oneself, taking care, or approaching a task with urgency and intensity.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r2.anchor: “Teşmîr-i sâk”, paçayı sıvamak veya çemremek, yerine göre toplanmak, hazırlanmak, mahzurdan sakınarak cidd ü ihtimam ile işe sıvanmak, şiddet ibraz etmek

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r3.claim: 'Uncovering the shin' depicts a hidden reality beginning to reveal itself clearly, from within outward or from below upward, with forceful emotional impact.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r3.anchor: “keşf-i sâk” veya “keşf an sâk” mestur bir hakikatin, içerden dışarıya, aşağıdan yukarıya doğru bir uçtan kendini vuzuh ile basar

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r4.claim: Expressions of the shin becoming visible can share the sense of clarity yet differ in emotional effect; the effect depends on the reality revealed and the observer's relation to it.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r4.anchor: “Harb sâkını keşfetti”, “falan kahraman baldırını açıverdi” denilmekle “zafer sâkını açtı, murad bir uçtan kendini gösterdi

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r5.claim: The Qur'an's image of Bilqis exposing her shins in 27:44 signifies her weakness and vulnerability, not her strength.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r5.anchor: Belkıs’ın baldırlarını açması onun kuvvetini değil, zaafını kusurunu anlatmıştı

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r6.speaker: Keşşâf
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r6.claim: Al-Kashshaf's brief discussion points to both aspects of the expression: its figurative usage and its intensity.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r6.anchor: Keşşâf’ın kısaca geçen beyânâtında bu iki cihete de işaret vardır.

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r7.speaker: Rebî‘ b. Enes
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r7.claim: Rebi b. Anas glosses the day as the time when the covering is uncovered and the veil lifted; Elmalılı reports this through Abd b. Humayd as cited by Alusi.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r7.anchor: Rebî‘b. Enes demiştir ki: “O gün gıtâ keşfolunacağı, perdenin açılacağı gündür.

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r8.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported by Bayhaqi to explain the phrase as the disclosure of the matter and the appearance of deeds.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r8.anchor: Beyhakī de İbn Abbas’tan حِيْنَ يُكْشَفُ الأَْمْرُ وَتـَبْدُو الأَْعْمَال emr keşf olunup

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r9.speaker: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r9.claim: Sa'id b. Jubayr rejects attributing a literal shin to God and says that only a severe matter is uncovered; Elmalılı says the hadith should be understood likewise.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r9.anchor: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr, bu âyette “sâk”ın Allah teâlâ’ya izâfetini inkâr etmiş

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r10.claim: Elmalılı understands the uncovering as God's reality or judgment beginning to appear from the unseen into the visible world, awaited by believers and dreaded by criminals.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r10.anchor: biz burada يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَن سَاقٍۢ kavl-i celîlinde “keşf-i sâk”tan müslimin imanıyla beklediği, mücrimin kaçındığı Hakk’ın veya hükm-i Hakk’ın perde-i gaybdan sâha-i şuhûda kendini bir uçtan göstermeye başlaması

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r11.claim: The terrifying force of the disclosure is painful humiliation and crushing dread for criminals, but an enticing joy and honor for Muslims.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r11.anchor: mücrimlere mahz-ı elem olan hevl-engiz bir kahr u tezlil, müslimlere de aynı hâile içinde murad kapısını açan câzibeli bir şevk ve izzet heyecânı

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r12.claim: The verse is a severe warning to the criminals and their partners, while its address to the Prophet frames it as promise and glad tidings for believers.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r12.anchor: bu âyet müslimlere bir va‘d ü tebşir olmak üzere Peygamber’e hitab siyâkında vârid olmuştur

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r13.claim: Elmalılı says فَلْيَأْتُوا is attached to يَوْمَ, though it may instead attach to an omitted اُذْكُرْ or to the later تَرْهَقُهُمْ.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r13.anchor: اُذْكُرْ gibi bir mahzûfa da yahut gelecek تَرْهَقُهُمْ fiiline de ta‘alluk edebilir.

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r14.claim: At the resurrection the deniers are summoned, individually or in groups, to submit and prostrate as a rebuke, but cannot raise their heads or bend their backs.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r14.anchor: ne başlarını kaldırabilecekler, ne bellerini eğebilecekler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r1.speaker: مفسرlerin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r1.claim: Most exegetes understand “the day” as Judgment Day, when exceptionally severe and distressing events occur.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r1.anchor: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğuna göre buradaki “gün”den maksat, son derece şiddetli ve sıkıntılı olayların ortaya çıkacağı kıyamet günüdür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r2.claim: The idiom literally means “the shin is uncovered”; it can signify undertaking a serious, difficult matter, truth becoming clear, or an event drawing near, and here evokes Judgment Day's hardships.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r2.anchor: lafzan “incikten açılır” şeklinde tercüme edilmekte; bununla ciddi, önemli ve güç bir işe girişilmesi veya bütün hakikatlerin açıkça ortaya çıkması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r3.claim: The expression in this verse especially refers to Judgment Day and its hardships.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r3.anchor: Âyette bu deyim özellikle kıyamet gününü ve o günün sıkıntılarını ifade etmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r4.claim: At the gathering, people commissioned by God call them to prostrate so they can escape that day's distress.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r4.anchor: mahşerde Allah tarafından görevlendirilenler onları Allah’a secde etmeye çağırırlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r5.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r5.claim: Razi says unbelievers will be summoned to prostrate as a means of reproach and rebuke because they did not prostrate in worldly life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r5.anchor: Râzî’ye göre inkârcılar dünyada Allah’a secde etmedikleri için âhirette kınanmak ve azarlanmak maksadıyla secdeye çağrılacaklardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r6.claim: A hadith says men and women prostrate; those who prostrated ostentatiously in life will wish to prostrate then but will be unable to bend.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r6.anchor: Hadiste buyurulduğu üzere erkek kadın herkes Allah’a secde eder; dünyada gösteriş için secde etmiş olanlar da secde etmek isterler, fakat eğilemezler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r7.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r7.claim: A further narration says that even unbelievers will wish to prostrate but will lack the ability to do so.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r7.anchor: inkârcıların da secde etmek isteyecekleri fakat buna güçlerinin yetmeyeceği haber verilmiştir (Şevkânî, V, 317)

BAQILLANI:v1p4/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p4/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p4/r1.claim: Bāqillānī says some current heretics compare the Qur’an with poetry and other speech; earlier Quraysh opponents often later recognized its truth and repented, while present unbelief is more entrenched.
BAQILLANI:v1p4/r1.anchor: وقد سبقهم إلى عظم ما يقولونه إخوانهم من ملحدة قريش وغيرهم إلا أن أكثر من كان طعن فيه في أول أمره استبان رشده

BAQILLANI:v1p4/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p4/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p4/r2.claim: Explaining the Qur’an’s inimitability deserved more attention than the technical debates and fine grammatical topics on which scholars spent their effort.
BAQILLANI:v1p4/r2.anchor: فهو أحق بكثير مما صنفوا فيه من القول

BAQILLANI:v1p4/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p4/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p4/r3.claim: Neglecting a convincing account of the miracle led some writers toward Brahmanism: they saw their peers’ verbal skill but found arguments for the Qur’an’s inimitability incomplete and poorly ordered.
BAQILLANI:v1p4/r3.anchor: وقد قصر بعضهم في هذه المسألة حتى أدى ذلك إلى تحول قوم منهم إلى مذاهب البراهمة فيها

BAQILLANI:v1p4/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p4/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p4/r4.claim: Some scholars can be excused for neglect because this subject can be mastered only after learning demanding, subtle prerequisites.
BAQILLANI:v1p4/r4.anchor: وقد يعذر بعضهم في تفريط يقع منه فيه وذهاب عنه لأن هذا الباب مما لا يمكن إحكامه إلا بعد التقدم في أمور شريفة المحل عظيمة المقدار

BAQILLANI:v1p4/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p4/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p4/r5.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ’s book on Qur’anic composition added nothing beyond earlier theologians and did not clarify the subject’s most obscure points.
BAQILLANI:v1p4/r5.anchor: وقد صنف الجاحظ في نظم القرآن كتابا لم يزد فيه على ما قاله المتكلمون قبله ولم يكشف عما يلتبس

BAQILLANI:v1p60/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p60/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p60/r1.claim: Qur’anic verse endings are distinctive and unlike familiar sajʿ, poetry, and ordinary speech; Abu Ṭālib’s patterned address to Sayf ibn Dhī Yazan exemplifies ordinary sajʿ.
BAQILLANI:v1p60/r1.anchor: ومن جنس السجع المعتاد عندهم قول أبي طالب لسيف يبن ذي يزن أنبتك منبتا طابت أرومته وعزت جرثومته

BAQILLANI:v1p60/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p60/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p60/r2.claim: He rejects deriving sajʿ from the pigeon’s repeated call: repetition alone cannot define the form, or poetry would also count as sajʿ because its rhymes recur consistently.
BAQILLANI:v1p60/r2.anchor: ولا معنى لقولهم إن ذلك مشتق من ترديد الحمامة صوتها على نسق واحد وروي غير مختلف لأن ما جرى هذا المجرى لا يبني على الاشتقاق وحده

BAQILLANI:v1p60/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p60/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p60/r3.claim: He rejects the claim that Moses and Aaron’s changing order serves rhyme; varied retellings of one story with different wording but the same meaning are difficult and display eloquence and inability to imitate.
BAQILLANI:v1p60/r3.anchor: وأما ما ذكروه من تقديم موسى على هارون عليهما السلام في موضع وتأخيره عنه في موضع لمكان السجع وتساوي مقاطع الكلام فليس بصحيح

BAQILLANI:v1p60/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p60/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p60/r4.claim: If opponents could match the Qur’an, they would have retold its stories in equivalent wording; the challenge to produce a like discourse therefore demonstrates inimitability.
BAQILLANI:v1p60/r4.anchor: ولو كان فيهم تمكن من المعارضة لقصدوا تلك القصة وعبروا عنها بألفاظ لهم تؤدي تلك المعاني ونحوها

BAQILLANI:v1p159/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r1.claim: The Qur’an has a distinct, unmatched style; Bāqillānī sets it against Imruʾ al-Qays’s celebrated opening couplets to expose their weaknesses.
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r1.anchor: ونظم القرآن جنس متميز وأسلوب متخصص وقبيل عن النظير متخلص فإذا شئت أن تعرف عظم شأنه فتأمل ما نقوله في هذا الفصل لامريء القيس

BAQILLANI:v1p159/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r2.speaker: الذين يتعصبون له
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r2.claim: The poem’s defenders call the passage ingenious because it combines stopping, weeping, recalling the beloved and home, and expressing pain in a couplet.
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r2.anchor: الذين يتعصبون له ويدعون محاسن الشعر ويقولون هذا من البديع لأنه وقف واستوقف وبكى واستبكى وذكر العهد والمنزل

BAQILLANI:v1p159/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r3.claim: Asking an untroubled listener to stop and weep for another’s beloved is illogical; seeking sympathy makes sense only when a friend weeps in response to the speaker’s grief.
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r3.anchor: فأول ذلك انه استوقف من يبكي لذكر الحبيب وذكراه لا تقتضي بكاء الخلى وإنما يصح طلب الإسعاد في مثل هذا

BAQILLANI:v1p159/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r4.claim: If the listener is also the beloved’s lover, the request becomes intelligible but makes the speaker ridiculous for inviting a rival to share flirtation and desire.
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r4.anchor: فإن كان المطلوب وقوفه وبكاؤه أيضا عاشقا صح الكلام من وجه وفسد المعنى من وجه آخر لأنه من السخف أن لا يغار على حبيبه

BAQILLANI:v1p159/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r5.claim: Listing all the named places adds no useful meaning; a few would identify the setting, so the rest is needless verbosity.
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r5.anchor: ثم في البيتين ما لا يفيد من ذكر هذه المواضع وتسمية هذه الأماكن من الدخول وحومل وتوضح والمقراة وسقط اللوى

BAQILLANI:v1p159/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r6.speaker: الأصمعي
