BAQILLANI:v1p159/r6.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī praises the line about the trace not being erased because the surviving ruins can still be seen and mourned.
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r6.anchor: ذكر الأصمعي من محاسنه انه باق فنحن نحزن على مشاهدته

BAQILLANI:v1p159/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r7.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r7.claim: Bāqillānī argues that a devoted lover would feel renewed longing if the traces were erased; al-Aṣmaʿī invents a benefit to defend what is really filler, without repairing the flaw.
BAQILLANI:v1p159/r7.anchor: وهذا بأن يكون من مساويه أولى لأنه إن كان صادق الود فلا يزيده عفاء الرسوم إلا جدة عهد وشدة وجد

BURHAN:v2p84/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p84/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p84/r1.claim: The idiom of rolling up one’s shins originated in facing a grave task that requires exertion, and figuratively conveys hardship.
BURHAN:v2p84/r1.anchor: وأصل هذا أن الرجل إذا وقع في أمر عظيم يحتاج إلى معاناة

BURHAN:v2p82/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p82/r9.speaker: قتادة
BURHAN:v2p82/r9.claim: Qatada interprets عن ساق as referring to severe hardship.
BURHAN:v2p82/r9.anchor: قال قتادة عن شدة وقال إبراهيم النخعي

BURHAN:v2p82/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p82/r10.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
BURHAN:v2p82/r10.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha‘i interprets عن ساق as referring to a great event, supporting the sense with a line describing war rising to its ساق.
BURHAN:v2p82/r10.anchor: وقال إبراهيم النخعي ( 3 ) أي عن أمر عظيم قال الشاعر

BURHAN:v2p178/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p178/r1.speaker: المحققون
BURHAN:v2p178/r1.claim: The careful scholars avoid calling particles extra in the Qur'an because “extra” implies that a word has no meaning, which is impossible of God's speech.
BURHAN:v2p178/r1.anchor: والذي عليه المحققون تجنب هذا اللفظ في القرآن اذ الزائد ما لا معنى له وكلام الله منزه عن ذلك

BURHAN:v2p178/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p178/r2.speaker: داود الظاهري
BURHAN:v2p178/r2.claim: Dawud al-Zahiri and other early authorities deny that the Qur'an contains extra connective particles; most grammarians take the opposite position.
BURHAN:v2p178/r2.anchor: وممن نص على منع ذلك في المتقدمين الإمام داود الظاهري

BURHAN:v2p178/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p178/r3.speaker: أبو سليمان
BURHAN:v2p178/r3.claim: Some companions report Abu Sulayman saying that there is no particle of connection in the Qur'an.
BURHAN:v2p178/r3.anchor: وروى بعض اصحابنا عن أبي سليمان انه كان يقول ليس في القرآن صلة بوجه

BURHAN:v2p178/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p178/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p178/r10.claim: The author classifies reading يوم يكشف عن ساق literally as a strained interpretation.
BURHAN:v2p178/r10.anchor: والثالث ما استعير فيه كقوله تعالى

BURHAN:v3p433/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p433/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p433/r1.claim: He recounts a story in which Abu Tammam is asked for water of blame and replies by asking for a feather from the wing of humility.
BURHAN:v3p433/r1.anchor: فيقال إنه أرسل إليه قارورة وقال ابعث إلى فيها شيئا من ماء الملام فأرسل أبو تمام أن ابعث لي ريشة من جناح الذل

BURHAN:v3p433/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p433/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p433/r2.claim: Zarkashī says the story is not a sound parallel: a wing suits humility, whereas water does not suit blame in the same way.
BURHAN:v3p433/r2.anchor: وهذا لا يصح له تعلق به والفرق بين التشبيهين ظاهر لأنه ليس جعل الجناح للذل كجعل الماء للملام

BURHAN:v3p433/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p433/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p433/r3.claim: The wing of humility is apt because a tired bird spreads its wing and drops to earth, while a submissive person lowers head and hands like wings.
BURHAN:v3p433/r3.anchor: فإن الطائر إذا وهى وتعب بسط جناحه وألقى نفسه إلى الأرض وللإنسان أيضا جناح فإن يديه جناحاه

BURHAN:v3p433/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p433/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p433/r4.claim: The water of blame lacks the fitting resemblance that makes the wing of humility an apt metaphor.
BURHAN:v3p433/r4.anchor: وأما ماء الملام فليس كذلك في مناسبة التشبيه فلذلك استهجن منه

BURHAN:v3p433/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p433/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p433/r5.claim: He offers a possible analysis: blame is implicitly likened to a bitter drink vessel, then borrowed as its water, making the imaginative metaphor derivative of an implicit metaphor.
BURHAN:v3p433/r5.anchor: قد يقال إن الاستعارة التخييلية فيه تابعة للاستعارة بالكناية فإن تشبيه الملام بظرف الشراب لاشتماله على ما يكرهه الشارب لمرارته

BURHAN:v3p433/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p433/r6.speaker: الإمام فخر الدين
BURHAN:v3p433/r6.claim: Fakhr al-Dīn says metaphor is not majāz because no transfer occurs; in reality it is a simile whose particle is omitted verbally and conceptually.
BURHAN:v3p433/r6.anchor: وقال الإمام فخر الدين ليس بمجاز لعدم النقل وفي الحقيقة هي تشبيه محذوف الأداة لفظا وتقديرا

BURHAN:v3p433/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p433/r7.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v3p433/r7.claim: Some define metaphor as asserting an object's literal meaning for heightened simile, as in saying their stick split for their division or war uncovered a shin.
BURHAN:v3p433/r7.anchor: حدها بعضهم بادعاء معنى الحقيقة في الشيء مبالغة في التشبيه كقولهم انشقت عصاهم إذا تفرقوا وذلك للعصا لا للقوم ويقولون كشفت الحرب عن ساق

BURHAN:v3p433/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p433/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p433/r8.claim: An explicit comparison particle makes a simile clear; naming both terms without the particle is an emphatic simile, while naming only the borrowed image makes it metaphor.
BURHAN:v3p433/r8.anchor: ويفترقان في أن التشبيه إذا ذكرت معه الأداة فلا خفاء أنه تشبيه وإن حذفت فهذا يلتبس بالاستعارة

ITQAN:v3p19/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p19/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p19/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the day of the trumpet or distress as a day of hardship and severity; the poem pictures war standing on its legs.
ITQAN:v3p19/r1.anchor:
( وقامت الحرب بنا على ساق )
قال ابن عباس هذا يوم كرب وشدة

ITQAN:v4p532#4/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p532#4/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p532#4/r4.claim: Abu Musa reports the Prophet interpreting the uncovering of the ساق as a great light before which people prostrate; the chain contains an unnamed transmitter.
ITQAN:v4p532#4/r4.anchor: عن أبي موسى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ﴿ يوم يكشف عن ساق ﴾ قال ( عن نور عظيم يخرون له سجدا

SULAMI:v2p345#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p345#3/r1.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p345#3/r1.claim: Jaʿfar interprets the uncovering as the terrors, hardships, Bridge, and Judgment; a believer preceded by divine care and mercy is spared these terrors, while one met with divine justice cannot prostrate and has a back hard as stone.
SULAMI:v2p345#3/r1.anchor: قال جعفر : عن الأهوال والشدائد والصراط والحساب وعبدي المؤمن الذي سبقت له عنايتي ورحمتي سالم من تلك الأهوال

SULAMI:v2p345#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p345#3/r2.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p345#3/r2.claim: When one saint meets another saint, hardships are unveiled from him.
SULAMI:v2p345#3/r2.anchor: قال جعفر : عن الأهوال والشدائد والصراط والحساب وعبدي المؤمن الذي سبقت له عنايتي

ITQAN:v2p334#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p334#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p334#2/r4.claim: يوم يكشف عن ساق means the Day of a severe, terrifying affair: the Resurrection.
ITQAN:v2p334#2/r4.anchor: ﴿ يوم يكشف عن ساق ﴾ هو الأمر الشديد المفظع من الهول يوم القيامة

ITQAN:v3p17/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p17/r1.speaker: غيره
ITQAN:v3p17/r1.claim: An unnamed interpreter glosses the attributes in the preceding discussion as God’s protection and guardianship.
ITQAN:v3p17/r1.anchor: وقال غيره المراد في الآيات كلاءته تعالى وحفظه

ITQAN:v3p17/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p17/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p17/r7.claim: Uncovering a ساق means facing a severe matter, as in the Arabic idiom that war stands upon a ساق.
ITQAN:v3p17/r7.anchor: ومن ذلك الساق في قوله ﴿ يوم يكشف عن ساق ﴾ ومعناه عن شدة وأمر عظيم كما يقال

ITQAN:v3p17/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p17/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p17/r8.claim: Asked about the verse, Ibn Abbas says obscure Qur’anic language should be sought in Arabic poetry, the Arabs’ archive; the excerpt introduces but does not quote his poetic evidence.
ITQAN:v3p17/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه سئل عن قوله ﴿ يوم يكشف عن ساق ﴾ قال إذا خفي عليكم شيء من القرآن فابتغوه في الشعر

ITQAN:v3p31/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p31/r3.speaker: العلماء
ITQAN:v3p31/r3.claim: Scholars say ambiguous passages impose interpretive effort that earns greater reward.
ITQAN:v3p31/r3.anchor: منها أنه يوجب المشقة في الوصول إلى المراد وزيادة المشقة توجب مزيد الثواب

ITQAN:v3p31/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p31/r4.speaker: العلماء
ITQAN:v3p31/r4.claim: Ambiguity invites adherents of different schools to study the Qur’an; clear passages then explain the ambiguous ones and lead mistaken readers toward truth.
ITQAN:v3p31/r4.anchor: فإذا كان مشتملا على المحكم والمتشابه طمع صاحب كل مذهب أن يجد فيه ما يؤيد مذهبه

ITQAN:v3p31/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p31/r5.speaker: العلماء
ITQAN:v3p31/r5.claim: Ambiguous passages require skills in language, grammar, rhetoric, and legal theory to interpret and weigh competing readings.
ITQAN:v3p31/r5.anchor: افتقر إلى العلم بطريق التأويلات وترجيح بعضها على بعض وافتقر في تعلم ذلك

ITQAN:v3p31/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p31/r6.speaker: العلماء
ITQAN:v3p31/r6.claim: Because ordinary people may mistake a nonbodily, nonspatial reality for nonexistence, revelation first addresses them with familiar approximate expressions mixed with clear truth.
ITQAN:v3p31/r6.anchor: فكان الأصلح أن يخاطبوا بألفاظ دالة على بعض ما يناسب ما توهموه وتخيلوه ويكون ذلك مخلوطا بما يدل على الحق الصريح

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r1.claim: The source gives proverbs, poetry, and explicit simile as examples of figurative representation, including the comparison of the addressee to night.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r1.anchor: وقوله السفر ميزان القوم وقول الأعرابي

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r2.claim: Readers who stop at a shared general label miss important distinctions; fine inquiry is needed to see where cases meet and where they diverge.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r2.anchor: الأمور التي تلتقي عند الجملة وتتباين لدى التفصيل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r3.claim: The natural order is to discuss literal and figurative usage, then simile and representation, then metaphor: metaphor is broader, and simile is its basis.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r3.anchor: أن المجاز أعم من الاستعارة والواجب في قضايا المراتب أن نبدأ بالعام قبل الخاص

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r4.claim: Despite that logical order, the author begins with metaphor because circumstances call for it, then promises to return to the other topics and complete the discussion.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p20/r4.anchor: إلا أن ههنا أمورا اقتضت أن تقع البداية بالاستعارة وبيان صدر منها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p102/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p102/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p102/r1.claim: First impressions come through the senses and natural disposition before reasoning, so they are more intimate and familiar to the soul.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p102/r1.anchor: العلم الأول آتى النفس أولا من طريق الحواس والطباع ثم من جهة النظر والرويه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p102/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p102/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p102/r2.claim: A simile makes an abstract meaning familiar by translating it from pure thought into something sensed or naturally known, like introducing a stranger through a beloved friend or unveiling a hidden object.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p102/r2.anchor: فأنت إذن مع الشاعر وغير الشاعر إذا وقع المعنى في نفسك غير ممثل ثم مثله كمن يخبر عن شىء من وراء حجاب ثم يكشف عنه الحجاب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p102/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p102/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p102/r3.claim: Representation can support a strange, disputed claim: the poet says an exceptional person surpasses humanity as musk, though part of deer blood, has left the nature and qualities of blood.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p102/r3.anchor: فإن تفق الأنام وأنت منهم فإن المسك بعض دم الغزال

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p324/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p324/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p324/r1.claim: In ‘making the earth’s delight life,’ the metaphor lies in the noun ‘life’ itself; it need not be attributed to the earth as a real life it possesses through another source.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p324/r1.anchor: اثبت بهجة الأرض حياة أو جعلها حياة أفلا ترى المجاز قد ظهر لك في الحياة من غير أن أضفتها إلى شيء

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p324/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p324/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p324/r2.claim: Lexical metaphor assigns a word a different but intelligible meaning, as when ‘life’ is used for knowledge; the transferred name still conveys a rational quality.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p324/r2.anchor: فنحن إذا تجوزنا في الحياة فأردنا بها العلم فقد أودعنا الاسم معنى

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p324/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p324/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p324/r3.claim: In ‘spring made the flowers,’ the verb is not transferred to a new intelligible sense; spring is only imagined as causing what appears with it, so this is an attribution of agency, not a lexical metaphor.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p324/r3.anchor: لما كان النور لا يوجد إلا بوجود الربيع توهم للربيع تأثير في وجوده فاثبت له ذلك اثبات الحكم أو الوصف

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r1.claim: Calling Zayd like a lion is a plain simile; saying it is as though Zayd were the lion intensifies the image and suggests exceptional bravery and fearlessness.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r1.anchor: فإنك تقول : زيد كالأسد ، أو شبيه بالأسد . فتجد ذلك كله تشبيها غفلا ساذجا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r2.claim: Saying that the lion will meet you in Zayd moves from imagined likeness to certainty and heightens the praise.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r2.anchor: فيخرج الأمر على حد التوهم إلى حد اليقين

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r3.claim: An unnamed poet's line comparing the addressee's hands with a lion's hands presents the comparison in a more artful image than the preceding formulations.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r3.anchor: أأن أرعشت كفا أبيك وأصبحت يداك يدي ليث فإنك غالبه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r4.claim: Arṭāh ibn Suhayya surpasses the earlier examples: his image makes the encounter cause the viewer to forget weapons and recognize the lion's brow.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r4.anchor: إن تلقني لا ترى غيري بناظرة تنس السلاح وتعرف جبهة الأسد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r5.claim: People can know a truth by introspection while finding it difficult to explain or prove in words.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r5.anchor: أن من الباطل والمحال ما يعلم الإنسان بطلانه واستحالته بالرجوع إلى النفس

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r6.speaker: المتعلقون بأمر اللفظ
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r6.claim: The opponents argue that an explanation must convey every meaning of what it explains, so a poem cannot exceed its prose interpretation in meaning and any remaining merit must be in wording.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r6.anchor: لا تلقي إلى أحد من المتعلقين بأمر اللفظ كلمة مما نحن فيه إلا كان هذا أول كلامه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r7.claim: Jurjani rejects that argument because it assumes there is no difference between the forms meanings take in metaphor and direct speech; it would also deny the greater force commonly granted to metaphor.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p312/r7.anchor: حتى يطلبوا ما أطبق عليه العقلاء من أن المجاز يكون أبدا أبلغ من الحقيقة

DAMGHANI:v1p253/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r4.claim: In the phrase about uncovering a ساق, sāq means hardship or distress.
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r4.anchor: الساق الشدة قوله تعالى في سورة القلم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p340#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p340#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p340#2/r1.claim: Sāq is the familiar leg; a plant’s branch is also called its sāq.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p340#2/r1.anchor: الأصل في الساق : العضو المعروف ، وكل نبات له غصن فغصنه ساقه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p340#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p340#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p340#2/r3.claim: Sāq can mean severity or hardship.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p340#2/r3.anchor: والثاني : الشدة . ومنه قوله تعالى في نون

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p481/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p481/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p481/r1.claim: Uncovering a ساق means that a matter has become severe; an unnamed poet says a year exposed its ساق, and Arabic says war stood on a ساق.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p481/r1.anchor: في سنة قد كشفت عن ساقها ... حمراء تبري اللحم عن عراقها (2)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p481/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p481/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p481/r2.claim: In the poem, ʿirāq is the plural of ʿirq, and al-ʿirāq means bones.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r1.claim: Arabic metaphor transfers a word to something linked by cause, adjacency, or resemblance.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r1.anchor: فالعرب تستعير الكلمة فتضعها مكان الكلمة، إذا كان المسمى بها بسبب من الأخرى، أو مجاورا لها، أو مشاكلا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r2.speaker: رؤية بن العجاج
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r2.claim: The plant may be called an anwaʾ because it is attributed to the rainy constellation; Ruʾba's line uses anwaʾ for vegetation.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r2.anchor: قال رؤية بن العجاج : وجف أنواء السحاب المرتزق أي جف البقل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r3.claim: Rain is called sky because it descends from the sky; the idiom about treading the sky uses it for rain.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r3.anchor: ويقولون للمطر: سماء، لأنه من السماء ينزل، فيقال: ما زلنا نطأ السماء حتى أتيناكم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r4.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r4.claim: The anonymous poet uses falling sky to mean rain, which people graze even when its recipients are angry.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r4.anchor: قال الشاعر : إذا سقط السماء بأرض قوم ... رعيناه وإن كانوا غضابا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r5.claim: The earth is said to laugh when it sprouts, since flowers emerge like teeth showing in a smile; a split palm spathe is also called laughter.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r5.anchor: ويقولون: ضحكت الأرض: إذا أنبتت، لأنها تبدي عن حسن النبات، وتنفتق عن الزهر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r6.claim: A flower is said to smile at the sun because it turns along with it.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r6.anchor: ويقال: النور يضاحك الشمس، لأنه يدور معها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r7.speaker: الأعشى
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r7.claim: Al-Aʿsha's garden poem uses yuḍāḥiku for a star or blossom facing the sun.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r7.anchor: وقال الأعشى يذكر روضة : يضاحك الشمس منها كوكب شرق

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r8.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r8.claim: The anonymous poet's cloud laughter means it cracks with lightning, while its weeping means rain.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r8.anchor: وقال آخر : وضحك المزن بها ثم بكى يريد بضحكه انعقاقه بالبرق، وببكائه: المطر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r9.claim: ʿIrq al-qirba means hardship: a waterskin carrier strains until sweat runs down his forehead; ʿirq al-jabin is a parallel idiom.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r9.anchor: وأصل هذا أن حامل القربة يتعب في نقلها حتى يعرق جبينه، فاستعير عرقها في موضع الشدة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r10.claim: Qatada explains uncovering the shin as the onset of a severe affair.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r10.anchor: أي عن شدة من الأمر، كذلك قال قتادة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r11.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r11.speaker: ابراهيم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r11.claim: Ibrahim glosses the phrase as referring to a great affair.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r12.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r12.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r12.claim: A person confronting a grave task bares his shins and exerts himself; the shin is therefore transferred to hardship.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r12.anchor: إذا وقع في أمر عظيم يحتاج إلى معاناته والجد فيه- شمر عن ساقه، فاستعيرت الساق في موضع الشدة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r13.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r13.speaker: دريد بن الصمة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r13.claim: Duraid's line depicts an exposed half-shin as a sign of endurance in difficult work.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r13.anchor: وقال دريد بن الصمة : كميش الإزار خارج نصف ساقه ... صبور على الجلاء طلاع أنجد

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r14.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r14.speaker: الهذلي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r14.claim: The Hudhali poet's raised garment exposing the shin illustrates readiness to exert oneself in hardship.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p88/r14.anchor: وقال الهذلي : وكنت إذا جاري دعا لمضوفة ... أشمر حتى ينصف الساق مئزري

NAHHAS:v5p14/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p14/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p14/r1.claim: The communal reading is the sound basis; other readings remain solitary even when chains are sound.
NAHHAS:v5p14/r1.anchor: هذه القراءة التي عليها جماعة الحجة وما يروى من غيرها يقع فيه الاضطراب

NAHHAS:v5p14/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p14/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p14/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās read تكشف and explained it as the Resurrection or Hour in its severity; al-Naḥḥās calls the chain sound.
NAHHAS:v5p14/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قرأ ( يوم تكشف عن ساق ) يريد القيامة والساعة لشدتها

NAHHAS:v5p14/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p14/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p14/r3.claim: Another report gives Ibn ʿAbbās's reading نكشف with nūn.
NAHHAS:v5p14/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قرأ ( يوم نكشف عن ساق ) بالنون

NAHHAS:v5p14/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p14/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
NAHHAS:v5p14/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd is reported to read نكشف with nūn and, in a second report, يكشف with active ya and kasra on shīn.
NAHHAS:v5p14/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه قرأ ( يوم نكشف عن ساق ) بالنون

NAHHAS:v5p14/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p14/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
NAHHAS:v5p14/r5.claim: Another Ibn Masʿūd report reads يكشف with fatḥa on yāʾ and kasra on shīn.
NAHHAS:v5p14/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه قرأ ( يوم يكشف عن ساق ) بفتح الياء وكسر الشين

NAHHAS:v5p14/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p14/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p14/r6.claim: Exegetes generally understand ساق as severity, a familiar Arabic idiom; another possible sense is people uncovering their shanks in distress.
NAHHAS:v5p14/r6.anchor: والذي عليه أهل التفسير أن المعنى يوم يكشف عن شدة وذلك معروف في كلام العرب

NAHHAS:v5p14/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p14/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p14/r7.claim: Another possibility is that people uncover their shanks because of their distress, a known Arabic usage.
NAHHAS:v5p14/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى يوم يكشف الناس عن سوقهم لشدة ما هم فيه

NAHHAS:v5p14/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p14/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p14/r8.claim: ساق is feminine and its diminutive takes tāʾ.

NAHHAS:v5p14/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p14/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p14/r9.claim: One view says they are summoned to reproach them for refusing useful prostration in worldly life; now it cannot benefit them because the afterlife is no trial.
NAHHAS:v5p14/r9.anchor: قيل إنما يدعون إلى السجود ليوبخوا بذلك فيقال لهم قد دعيتم إلى السجود

NAHHAS:v5p14/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p14/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p14/r10.claim: Another view says their backs stiffen as punishment and prevent prostration.
NAHHAS:v5p14/r10.anchor: وقيل بل تجف أصلابهم عقوبة فلا يستطيعون السجود

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r1.claim: The temporal phrase may depend on فليأتوا, be an object of implied اذكر, be an adverb with an omitted predicate, or attach to خاشعة; Abu al-Baqāʾ considers the last, which the author finds remote.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r1.anchor: منصوب بقوله " فليأتوا " أو بإضمار اذكر، فيكون مفعولا به أو بمحذوف، وهو ظرف

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r2.claim: In the passive reading, عن ساق occupies the position of the passive subject.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r2.anchor: و " عن ساق " قائم مقام الفاعل، وابن مسعود وابن أبي عبلة

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن أبي عبلة
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read يكشف with yāʾ as an active verb, with God as its subject.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r3.anchor: وابن مسعود وابن أبي عبلة " يكشف " بالياء من تحت مبنيا للفاعل وهو الله

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وعبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAbd Allāh also read نكشف with an active first-person plural.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعبد الله أيضا " نكشف " بكسر النون

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported to read تكشف actively with a feminine subject, the severity or the Hour.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس " تكشف " بالتاء من فوق مبنيا للفاعل، أي: الشدة والساعة

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r6.claim: A passive feminine تكشف is also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās; the author finds it problematic unless an implicit feminine subject, severity, is understood.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r6.anchor: وعنه كذلك أيضا مبنيا للمفعول وهي/ مشكلة؛ لأن التأنيث لا معنى له هنا

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows feminine تكشف in either the active or passive and takes its subject as the Hour or the situation becoming severe.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " وتكشف بالتاء مبنيا للفاعل والمفعول جميعا. والفعل للساعة، أو للحال

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r8.claim: Another reading derives from أكشف, meaning to enter into exposure; أكشف الرجل describes an upper lip turning up and exposing what lies beneath.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r8.anchor: وقرىء " يكشف " بضم الياء أو التاء وكسر الشين، من " أكشف " إذا دخل في الكشف

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r9.claim: Uncovering the ساق is a well-established Arabic metaphor for severe distress, as Arab verse and prose usage confirms.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r9.anchor: وكشف الساق كناية عن الشدة، لا يمتري في ذلك من ذاق طعم الكلام

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r10.speaker: الراجز
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r10.claim: A rajaz poet uses كشف عن ساقها for the severity of a harsh year, witnessing the idiom's sense of hardship.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r10.anchor:
قال الراجز:
4309 عجبت من نفسي ومن إشفاقها

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r11.speaker: حاتم الطائي
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r11.claim: Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī applies the idiom to war becoming severe.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r11.anchor:
وقال حاتم الطائي:
4310 أخو الحرب إن عضت به الحرب عضها

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r12.speaker: آخر
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r12.claim: An unnamed poet says war uncovered its ساق and open evil appeared, another witness for the hardship idiom.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r12.anchor:
وقال آخر:
4311 كشفت لهم عن ساقها

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r13.speaker: آخر
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r13.claim: An unnamed poet tells hearers to gird themselves when war raises its ساق, using the phrase for hardship.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r13.anchor:
وقال آخر:
4312 قد شمرت عن ساقها فشدوا

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r14.speaker: آخر
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r14.claim: Another anonymous line says war has come upon them with its ساق raised, continuing Arabic usage for a grave crisis.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r14.anchor:
وقال آخر:
4313 صبرا أمام إنه شر باق

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains uncovering the ساق and showing the خدام as metaphors for grave difficulty, originating in panic, defeat, and women baring their legs in battle; the author praises the account.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r15.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " الكشف عن الساق والإبداء عن الخدام مثل في شدة الأمر وصعوبة الخطب.

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r16.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r16.speaker: ابن قيس الرقيات
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r16.claim: Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt's verse uses إبداء عن خدام to evoke battle's terror distracting an old man from his sons.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r16.anchor:
وقال ابن قيس الرقيات:
4314 تذهل الشيخ عن بنيه وتبدي

SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r17.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r17.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r17.claim: The author treats exegetical claims and the report of Ibn Masʿūd and similar reports as figurative interpretations of the phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:68:42/r17.anchor: وما أورده أهل التفسير فإنه مؤول وكذلك حديث ابن مسعود ونحوه

ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r2.claim: The challenge is for them to bring their alleged partners on the Day of Resurrection.

ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r3.claim: In Arabic, uncovering a shin is an idiom for the disclosure of a grave or severe matter; the cited battle verse illustrates the idiom.
ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r3.anchor: ومعنى (يكشف عن ساق) في اللغة يكشف عن الأمر الشديد

ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the phrase as the disclosure of a severe matter.
ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس في قوله: (يكشف عن ساق) عن الأمر الشديد

ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the Merciful will uncover His shin: believers will prostrate to Him, while hypocrites' backs will become rigid, vertebra after vertebra, like skewers.
ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r5.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: يكشف الرحمن عن ساقه. فأما المؤمنون فيخرون له سجدا

ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r6.claim: Zajjāj takes the inability to prostrate and the following description of humbled eyes to refer to the hypocrites.
ZAJJAJ:v5p210/r6.anchor: هذا تأويل قوله (ويدعون إلى السجود فلا يستطيعون (42) خاشعة أبصارهم). يعني به المنافقون

ASAD-NOTES:68:40#n21/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:40#n21/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:40#n21/r1.claim: The image of the shin being bared means that people's innermost thoughts, feelings, and motivations will be exposed.
ASAD-NOTES:68:40#n21/r1.anchor: when man's innermost thoughts, feelings and motivations will be laid bare

ASAD-NOTES:68:40#n21/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:40#n21/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:40#n21/r2.claim: This exposure lays bare as indefensible and spiritually destructive the former claim that whatever is expedient is morally justifiable.
ASAD-NOTES:68:40#n21/r2.anchor: their erstwhile claim that whatever is "expedient" is morally justifiable (see note 19 above), shall be revealed in all its nakedness - namely, as something indefensible and spiritually destructive

ASAD-NOTES:68:40#n22/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:40#n22/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:40#n22/r1.claim: The call to prostrate means willingly and gladly humbling oneself before God.
ASAD-NOTES:68:40#n22/r1.anchor: I.e., willingly, gladly humbling themselves before Him

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p22/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p22/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p22/r1.claim: The author notes that mastery of Qur’anic inimitability requires advanced, subtle preparation; al-Jāḥiẓ’s book on Qur’anic order added little to earlier theologians and left much unexplained.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p22/r1.anchor: وقد صنف الجاحظ فى نظم القرآن كتاباً لم يزد فيه على ما قاله المتكلمون قبله

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p22/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p22/r2.speaker: أبو سليمان الخطابي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p22/r2.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī says many writers had discussed inimitability without reaching a satisfactory account because its nature and mode are difficult to know.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p22/r2.anchor: قد أكثر الناس الكلام فى هذا الباب قديما وحديثاً وذهبوا فيه كل مذهب من القول

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p22/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p22/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p22/r3.claim: The fourth century AH produced major works titled “Inimitability of the Qur’an,” including books by al-Rummānī, al-Khaṭṭābī, and al-Bāqillānī, plus a volume by Qāḍī ʿAbd al-Jabbār.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p22/r3.anchor: ومن أشهر ما وصل إلينا من مصنفاتهم فى الإعجاز

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p468/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p468/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p468/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the day’s uncovering of the shin as the severity of the afterlife and supports this sense with an Arab expression for war at full intensity.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p468/r5.anchor: قال: يا ابن عباس، أخبرني عن قول الله - عز وجل -: {يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ سَاقٍ} قال: عن شدة الآخرة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p468/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p468/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p468/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās cites a poetic expression that war has risen upon a shin as evidence for the idiom’s sense of intensity.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p468/r6.anchor: قد قامت الحرب بنا على ساقْ

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r1.claim: Uncovering the shin, like girding up in a similar context, is a metonym for the intensity of war, fear, and the grave affair of the gathering.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r1.anchor: الكشف عن الساق، والتشمير في مثل سياق آية القلم، عند اللغويين: كناية عن شدة الحرب والخوف

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r3.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that the phrase refers to the Resurrection and Hour because of their severity.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء في معنى آية القلم، عن ابن عباس: يريد القيامة والساعة لشدتها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r4.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports Companions and Successors interpreting it as the appearance of a grave ordeal; Ibn ʿAbbās calls it a day of war and hardship.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r4.anchor: وفي الطبري: قال جماعة من الصحابة والتابعين من أهل التأويل: يبدو عن أمر شديد

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r5.claim: Mujāhid’s reported gloss is that it is the most severe hour of the Day of Resurrection.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r5.anchor: وعن مجاهد عنه: هي أشد ساعة يوم القيامة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r6.claim: The reported explanations converge on a metonym for the terror of the gathering; al-Zamakhsharī likewise says the affair intensifies, with no literal shin being uncovered.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p469/r6.anchor: والأقوال فيها متقاربة، كناية عن هول الموقف يوم الحشر، والله أعلم

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351/r4.claim: The readers agree on the alif form of “sāq,” except for a reported hamza reading from Ibn Kathir.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351/r4.anchor: يقرأ بألف إجماع إلا ما روى من الهمز عن ابن كثير

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310/r1.claim: Ibrāhīm glosses “uncovering a ساق” as facing a grave matter, citing the Arabic expression that war has stood on a ساق.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310/r1.anchor: عن مغيرة عن إبراهيم في قوله تعالى ﴿ يوم يكشف عن ساق ﴾ قال عن أمر عظيم وقال قد قامت الحرب على ساق

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says every believer will prostrate, while the unbeliever's back will stiffen into a single bone.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس يكشف عن ساق فيسجد كل مؤمن ويقسو ظهر الكافر فيكون عظما واحدا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r1.claim: يوم may attach to فليأتوا under either of the two preceding parses, to an omitted imperative such as اذكر, or to خاشعة or ترهقهم.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r1.anchor: متعلق بقوله تعالى فليأتوا على الوجهين ويجوز تعلقه بمقدر كاذكر أو يكون كيت وكيت وقيل بخاشعة وقيل بترهقهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r2.claim: The majority take this as Judgment Day; ساق is the part above the foot, and uncovering or baring it is an idiom for an ordeal becoming severe, with its origin in women hiking their garments to flee in extreme danger.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r2.anchor: وأيا ما كان فالمراد بذلك اليوم عند الجمهور يوم القيامة والساق ما فوق القدم وكشفها والتشمير عنها مثل في شدة الأمر وصعوبة الخطب

ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r3.claim: Hatim’s poem and a rajaz verse show ساق used idiomatically for the onset of war and hardship, not necessarily a literal leg.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r3.anchor: ( أخو الحرب إن عضت به الحرب عضها وإن شمرت عن ساقها الحرب شمرا )

ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r4.speaker: مجاهد وإبراهيم النخعي وعكرمة وجماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r4.claim: Mujahid, Ibrahim al-Nakha‘i, Ikrima, and a group explain the phrase as an idiom for severe hardship; the interpretation is also reported from Ibn Abbas.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r4.anchor: وإلى نحو هذا ذهب مجاهد وإبراهيم النخعي وعكرمة وجماعة وقد روي أيضا عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r5.claim: Asked about the phrase, Ibn Abbas said that unclear Qur’anic wording should be sought in Arabic poetry, then cited a poem describing war rising upon a ساق; al-Hakim authenticated this report.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p34#5/r5.anchor: أخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم والحاكم وصححه والبيهقي في الأسماء والصفات من طريق عكرمة عنه أنه سئل عن ذلك فقال إذا خفي عليكم شيء من القرآن فابتغوه في الشعر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r1.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r1.claim: Another figurative reading takes ساق as the basis on which something stands; the day reveals the underlying reality of events, making their truths and origins visible. Al-Rabi ibn Anas says it is the day the veil is lifted.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r1.anchor: وقيل ساق الشيء أصله الذي به قوامه كساق الشجر وساق الإنسان والمراد يوم يكشف عن أصل الأمر فتظهر حقائق الأمور وأصولها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas is also reported to say that the phrase means the matter is disclosed and deeds appear.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r2.anchor: وكذا ما أخرجه البيهقي عن ابن عباس أيضا قال حين يكشف الأمر وتبدوا الأعمال

ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r3.claim: On the core-of-the-matter reading, ساق is an explicit metaphor and uncovering is another figurative expression or an intensifying extension; the indefinite noun may signal awe or greatness, though a fully parabolic reading does not parse each word separately.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r3.anchor: وفي الساق على هذا المعنى استعارة تصريحية وفي الكشف تجوز آخر أو هو ترشيح للاستعارة باق على حقيقته وتنكير ساق قيل للتهويل على الأول وللتعظيم على الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r4.claim: Some take the ساق to be God’s own ساق and classify the verse among the ambiguous texts, citing the hadith in which the Lord unveils His ساق and believers prostrate while pretenders cannot.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r4.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى أن المراد بالساق ساقه سبحانه وتعالى وإن الآية من المتشابه واستدل على ذلك بما أخرجه البخاري ومسلم والنسائي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r5.claim: Abu Sa‘id reports the Prophet saying that God unveils His ساق: believers prostrate, while those who bowed for show try and fail because their backs become rigid.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r5.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال سمعت النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يقول يكشف ربنا عن ساقه فيسجد له كل مؤمن ومؤمنة ويبقى من كان يسجد في الدنيا رياء وسمعة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r6.claim: Sa‘id ibn Jubayr angrily rejects the claim that God unveils a ساق; he interprets it as a grave matter and applies that sense to the hadith, whose attribution to God magnifies its severity and singularity.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r6.anchor: وأنكر ذلك سعيد بن جبير أخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عنه أنه سئل عن الآية فغضب غضبا شديدا وقال إن أقواما يزعمون أن الله سبحانه يكشف عن ساقه وإنما يكشف عن الأمر الشديد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r7.speaker: أرباب الباطن من الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r7.claim: Sufi esoteric authorities affirm the literal wording in an imaginal manifestation and apply that interpretation to Ibn Masud’s resurrection report, where God appears after people’s worldly objects of worship have been represented and is recognized by the sign of the ساق.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r7.anchor: وأرباب الباطن من الصوفية يقولون بالظاهر ويدعون أن ذلك عند التجلي الصوري وعليه حملوا أيضا ما أخرجه إسحاق بن راهويه في مسنده والطبراني والدارقطني في الرؤية

ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r8.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Masud describes the resurrection gathering, representations of what people worshipped, and Muslims awaiting their Lord; they recognize Him by the sign that He unveils the ساق. The report is among the ambiguous texts according to the Salaf.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r8.anchor: عن ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال يجمع الله الناس يوم القيامة وينزل الله في ظلل من الغمام فينادي مناد يا أيها الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r9.claim: Ibn Masud and Ibn Abi Abla read يكشف with an active yā, also transmitted from Ibn Abbas; Ibn Hurmuz reads نكشف with nūn, and another reading has passive-like intransitive يكشف from أكشف, meaning becoming exposed.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وابن أبي عبلة يكشف بفتح الياء مبينا الفاعل وهي رواية عن ابن عباس وقرأ ابن هرمز نكشف بالنون وقريء يكشف بالياء التحتية مضمومة وكسر الشين من أكشف

ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r10.claim: Other readings use feminine تكشف, referring actively to the understood Hour or state, or passively with that same referent; al-Alusi criticizes the resulting claim that the Hour itself uncovers its ساق as strained and grammatically awkward.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r10.anchor: وقريء تكشف بالتاء الفوقية والبناء للفاعل وهو ضمير الساعة المعلومة من ذكر يوم القيامة أو الحال المعلومة من دلالة الحال وبها والبناء للمفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r11.claim: Explaining the feminine reading as the Hour unveiling its own ساق requires an overstrained personification; making عن ساق an apposition after dropping the preposition violates Arabic syntax, while making it the passive agent conflicts with the verb’s gender agreement.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p35/r11.anchor: وتعقب بأنه يكون الأصل حينئذ يكشف الله الساعة عن ساقها مثلا ولو قيل ذلك لم يستقم لاستدعائه إبداء الساق وإذهاب الساعة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r1.claim: The summons to prostrate reproaches them for abandoning it in worldly life and makes them grieve over their neglect.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r1.anchor: توبيخا وتعنيفا على تركهم إياه في الدنيا وتحسيرا لهم على تفريطهم في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r2.claim: They cannot prostrate because their ability has been removed; their intention to prostrate remains, but they cannot carry it out.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r2.anchor: لزوال القدرة عليه وفيه دلالة على أنهم يقصدونه فلا يتأتى منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says their spines become rigid bones without joints, unable to bend when rising or lowering.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r3.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود تعقم أصلابهم أي ترد عظاما بلا مفاصل لا تنثني عند الرفع والخفض

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r4.claim: A hadith says the hypocrites’ and disbelievers’ spines become like ox horns, one solid bone.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r4.anchor: وفي حديث تصير أصلاب المنافقين والكفار كصياصي البقر عظما واحدا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r5.claim: The apparent caller is God, or an angel.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن الداعي الله تعالى أو الملك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r6.claim: An alternative says the summons is what they see of the believers prostrating.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r6.anchor: وقيل هو ما يرونه من سجود المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r7.claim: Abū Muslim places the disclosure in worldly life: since the Resurrection has no worship or obligation, it means either life’s final days when angels appear, or illness and senility.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r7.anchor: استدل أبو مسلم بهذه الآية على أن يوم الكشف في الدنيا قال لأنه تعالى قال ويدعون إلى السجود ويوم القيامة ليس فيه تعبد ولا تكليف

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects Abū Muslim’s argument by appeal to his preceding explanation of the post-resurrection summons and inability.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r1.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r1.claim: One parsing makes yawm an adverb modifying the command to bring their partners, who might benefit or intercede then.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r1.anchor: قيل: "يوم" ظرف لقوله فليأتوا بشركائهم، أي: فليأتوا بها في ذلك اليوم لتنفعهم وتشفع لهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r2.claim: One interpretation takes the uncovering of the ساق as the arrival of a terrible, intensely difficult event.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r2.anchor: قيل: عن أمر فظيع شديد، قال ابن عباس: هو أشد ساعة في القيامة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas calls it the most severe hour of the Resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو أشد ساعة في القيامة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r4.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains the phrase as the severity of the affair.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r4.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: "يوم يكشف عن ساق" عن شدة الأمر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba cites the Arab idiom of girding up one's garment for a grave effort, or war revealing its ساق when it intensifies.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: تقول العرب للرجل إذا وقع في أمر عظيم يحتاج فيه إلى الجد ومقاساة الشدة: شمر عن ساقه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r6.claim: Abu Saʿid reports the Prophet affirming that believers will see their Lord, comparing the sight to the sun or full moon in a clear sky; each community is then summoned to what it worshipped.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p198#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه أن أناسا في زمن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالوا: يا رسول الله هل نرى ربنا يوم القيامة؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p199#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p199#2/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p199#2/r1.claim: Abu Saʿid transmits the Prophet's statement that God uncovers His ساق; believing men and women prostrate, while showy worshippers cannot and their backs become rigid.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p199#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "يكشف ربنا عن ساقه فيسجد له كل مؤمن ومؤمنة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p199#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p199#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p199#2/r2.claim: The people unable to prostrate are disbelievers and hypocrites, whose backs become like cattle's horns, preventing them from bowing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p199#2/r2.anchor: يعني: الكفار والمنافقين تصير أصلابهم كصياصي البقر، فلا يستطيعون السجود.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r5.claim: Uncovering a ساق depicts an intensely difficult affair; the image originates in women hitching up their skirts while fleeing.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r6.speaker: حاتم
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r6.claim: Hatim's battle poem uses uncovering the ساق as an image for war's severe onset.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r6.anchor: قال حاتم. أخو الحرب إن عضت به الحرب عضها

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r7.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means the root and reality of the matter will be uncovered until it becomes visible, by analogy with a tree's or person's trunk.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r7.anchor: أو يوم يكشف عن أصل الأمر وحقيقته بحيث يصير عيانا مستعار من ساق الشجر وساق الإنسان

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r8.claim: The indefinite form of ساق conveys awe or magnification.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r9.claim: The verb is also read with tāʾ, in active or passive form, with the Hour or the circumstance as its subject.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r9.anchor: وقرىء «تكشف» و «تكشف» بالتاء على بناء الفاعل أو المفعول والفعل للساعة أو الحال

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r10.claim: If the scene is Judgment Day, the call rebukes them for neglecting prostration; if it is the moment of death, it calls them to prayers at their appointed times.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r10.anchor: توبيخا على تركهم السجود إن كان اليوم

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r11.claim: They cannot prostrate because its time has passed or their ability has disappeared.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:40-43/r11.anchor: لذهاب وقته أو زوال القدرة عليه

BINTSHATI:v2p67/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p67/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p67/r4.claim: The author attaches the temporal phrase “the day” to the preceding command: let them bring their partners, if truthful, on the day the shin is uncovered.
BINTSHATI:v2p67/r4.anchor: أي: فليأتوا بشركائهم، إن كانوا صادقين، يوم يكشف عن ساق

BINTSHATI:v2p68/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r3.claim: The author calls the interpretation as God’s literal leg one of the strangest reports and challenges the anthropomorphists who rely on it.

BINTSHATI:v2p68/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r4.claim: In Arabic usage, uncovering or tucking up the shin is a figurative expression for readiness, alarm, and the onset of severe hardship, especially war.
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r4.anchor: فهل أعوزهم من بيان العربية أنها ألفت مثل هذا الاستعمال المجازي: الكشف عن الساق، أو التشمير عنها

BINTSHATI:v2p68/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r5.speaker: الشاعر
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r5.claim: An unnamed poet uses uncovering the shin as an image of an approaching, destructive crisis.
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r5.anchor: قال الشاعر: كشفت لهم عن ساقها وبدا من الشر البوارح

BINTSHATI:v2p68/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r6.speaker: حاتم الطائي
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r6.claim: Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī’s line depicts war as biting back when it is pressed and as baring its shin when it intensifies.
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r6.anchor: وقال حاتم الطائي: أخو الحرب إن غضت به الحرب عضها وإن شمرت عن ساقها الحرب شمرا

BINTSHATI:v2p68/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r7.speaker: ابن قيس الرقيات
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r7.claim: Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt’s line has a woman’s attendants exposed when the crisis distracts the old man from his sons.
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r7.anchor: وقال ابن قيس الرقيات: تذهل الشيخ عن بنيه وتبدى عن خدام العقيلة العذراء

BINTSHATI:v2p68/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r8.speaker: الراجز
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r8.claim: A rajaz poet’s line says war has bared its shin and urges people to gird themselves and exert effort.
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r8.anchor: وقال الراجز: قد شمرت عن ساقها فشدوا وجدت الحرب بكم فجدوا

SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.claim: Ordinary vocatives are introduced by five forms: yā, ayā, hayā, ay, or a final alif, as in yā Ḥār ibn ʿAmr.
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.anchor: فأما الاسم غير المندوب فينبه بخمسة أشياء بيا وأيا وهيا وأى وبالألف

SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.claim: The four vocatives other than alif can prolong a call to someone far away, inattentive, or deeply asleep; these forms can serve where alif is used, but alif cannot serve in those cases.
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.anchor: يستعملونها إذا أرادوا أن يمدوا أصواتهم للشئ المتراخى عنهم

SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.claim: The long forms can also address someone nearby for emphasis; all five markers may be omitted when the addressee is treated as present and directly addressed.
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.anchor: كان صاحبك قريبا منك مقبلا عليك توكيدا

SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.claim: The vocative particle cannot be omitted with demonstratives because it replaces ay after its deletion; yā may be dropped with an indefinite in poetry, but Sībawayh calls this rare and weak.
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.anchor: الحرف الذي ينبه به لزم المبهم كأنه صار بدلا من أي

SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj omits yā in the poetic address jāri, intending yā jāriya; Sībawayh treats such deletion as uncommon and weak.
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.anchor: وقد يجوز حذف يا من النكرة

SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فأماالاسمغيرالمندوبفينبهبخمسةأش.claim: Yā is required with a person being implored or marveled at; lamentation uses yā and wā, with lengthening for a sung call to someone distant.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r1.claim: The interpretation “a great light before which they fall prostrate” does not conflict with the readings of severity or unveiling.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r1.anchor: عن نور عظيم يخرون له سجدا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r2.claim: Unveiling serves worship: prostration marks outward submission and signals the inward devotion it contains.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r2.anchor: ولما كان هذا الكشف الذي كشف لهم المعاني في هذا القرآن إنما هو لأجل العبادة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r3.claim: On that day the summons to prostrate rebukes and humiliates them for refusing it in earthly life; it is not a new act of worship or legal obligation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r3.anchor: توبيخا على تركه الآن وتنديما وتعنيفا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r4.claim: The passive construction signals their desire to submit and willingness to answer any caller.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r4.anchor: بانيا للمفعول دلالة على إرادتهم للانقياد ورغبتهم فيه من أي داع كان

BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r5.claim: Biqāʿī says legal responsibility ends only when each of the two groups enters its own abode.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r5.anchor: وهو دال على أن التكليف لا ينقطع إلا بدخول كل من الفريقين داره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r6.claim: Their backs and limbs become one unbending plane, so each attempt to prostrate turns them onto their backs.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r6.anchor: فكلما أرادوا أن يسجدوا انقلبوا على أقفائهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r7.claim: Biqāʿī says this matches an authentic hadith describing a heart-sick person whose back becomes one vertebra and who falls back whenever he tries to prostrate.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r7.anchor: مطابقة لما ورد في الحديث الصحيح على أن من كان في قلبه مرض في الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r8.claim: People are raised in the state in which they died and gathered in the state in which they were raised, good for good and evil for evil.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r8.anchor: يبعث المرء على ما مات عليه ويحشر على ما بعث عليه إن خيرا فخيرا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r14.claim: The passage uses iḥtibāk: inability in the first verse implies omitted ability in the second, while safety in the second implies omitted unsafety in the first.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r14.anchor: ذكر عدم الاستطاعة أولا دال على حذف الاستطاعة ثانيا

DURR-FULL:v8p253/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r1.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports that God unveils His ساق; believers prostrate, while those who prostrated for show cannot and their backs become rigid as one piece.
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: يكشف ربنا عن ساقه فيسجد له كل مؤمن ومؤمنة

DURR-FULL:v8p253/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r2.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra glosses the phrase as God unveiling His ساق.
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: يكشف الله عز وجل عن ساقه

DURR-FULL:v8p253/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd explains the phrase as God's two ساقs; Ibn Mandah suggests this may reflect Ibn Masʿūd's reading with an active verb form.
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: عن ساقيه تبارك وتعالى

DURR-FULL:v8p253/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r4.speaker: ابن منده
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r4.claim: Ibn Mandah suggests that Ibn Masʿūd read the verb with fatḥa on yāʾ and kasra on shīn.
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r4.anchor: قال ابن منده: لعله في قراءة ابن مسعود يكشف بفتح الياء وكسر الشين

DURR-FULL:v8p253/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r5.claim: Abū Mūsā reports that the phrase refers to a great light before people fall prostrate; al-Bayhaqī graded this report weak.
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r5.anchor: عن أبي موسى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: عن نور عظيم فيخرون له سجدا

DURR-FULL:v8p253/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r6.claim: Through Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, Ibn ʿAbbās explains the phrase as the disclosure of a great affair, using the idiom “war has risen to its ساق.”
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r6.anchor: من طريق إبراهيم النخعي في قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: قال ابن عباس يكشف عن أمر عظيم

DURR-FULL:v8p253/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says God unveils His ساق, believers prostrate, and the unbeliever's back becomes one bone.
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r7.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: يكشف عن ساقه فيسجد كل مؤمن ويعصو ظهر الكافر فيصير عظما واحدا

DURR-FULL:v8p253/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says unclear Qurʾānic expressions should be sought in Arabic poetry; the cited line uses “war stood on a ساق” to mean a day of distress and severity.
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه سئل عن قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: إذا خفي عليكم شيء من القرآن فابتغوه في الشعر

DURR-FULL:v8p253/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r9.claim: Answering Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq, Ibn ʿAbbās explains the phrase as the severity of the Hereafter and adduces the Arabic idiom “war has arisen on a ساق.”
DURR-FULL:v8p253/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس إن نافع بن الأزرق سأله عن قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: عن شدة الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v8p254/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the phrase as the severity of the Hereafter.
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: عن شدة الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v8p254/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r2.claim: Mujāhid explains it as the severity and gravity of the affair, adding that Ibn ʿAbbās called it the most severe hour of Judgment Day.
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: عن شدة الأمر وجده

DURR-FULL:v8p254/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the phrase means the Resurrection and Hour, whose severity is being emphasized.
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قرأ {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: يريد القيامة والساعة لشدتها

DURR-FULL:v8p254/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the affair is exposed and deeds become manifest; its uncovering marks entry into the afterlife and disclosure of the matter.
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: حين يكشف الأمر وتبدو الأعمال

DURR-FULL:v8p254/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r5.claim: Via ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to read “yawm takshifu ʿan sāq”; Abū Ḥātim explains that the Hereafter reveals what had been hidden.
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r5.anchor: قال: كان ابن عباس يقرأ يوم يكشف عن ساق بفتح التاء

DURR-FULL:v8p254/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r6.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r6.claim: ʿĀṣim recited the verb with yāʾ and a raised yāʾ vowel, as transmitted in the source's wording.
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r6.anchor: عن عاصم أنه قرأ {يوم يكشف عن ساق} بالياء ورفع الياء

DURR-FULL:v8p254/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r7.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r7.claim: ʿIkrima explains that Arabs said “war has uncovered a ساق” when battle and danger intensified; God describes the Day's severity in familiar language.
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة أنه سئل عن قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: إن العرب كانوا إذا اشتد القتال

DURR-FULL:v8p254/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r8.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr angrily rejects the claim that God unveils His ساق and insists that what is unveiled is the severe affair.
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير أنه سئل عن قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} فغضب غضبا شديدا وقال: إن أقواما يزعمون

DURR-FULL:v8p254/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r10.claim: Mujāhid says a hypocrite stands between every two believers at Judgment; believers prostrate, while hypocrites' backs stiffen, bringing rebuke, regret, and grief.
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد في الآية قال: أخبرنا أن بين كل مؤمنين منافقا يوم القيامة فيسجد المؤمنان

DURR-FULL:v8p256/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r1.claim: Mujāhid says the phrase refers to a tremendous tribulation.
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: عن بلاء عظيم

DURR-FULL:v8p256/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r2.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r2.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī explains it as an affair of extreme severity.
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r2.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: عن أمر عظيم الشدة

DURR-FULL:v8p256/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r3.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r3.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas describes the lifting of the veil: believers who trusted God prostrate, while those who did not believe cannot; they had been able to prostrate safely in worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r3.anchor: عن الغطاء فيقع من كان آمن به في الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v8p256/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r4.claim: Qatāda calls the unveiling a horrendous, momentous affair and reports that believers prostrate while hypocrites' backs stiffen; their prostration brings hypocrites humiliation and regret.
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: أمر فظيع جليل {ويدعون إلى السجود فلا يستطيعون} قال: ذلكم يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v8p256/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r6.speaker: كعب الحبر
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r6.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār swears that the verses were revealed about the five obligatory prayers when they are called.
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r6.anchor: عن كعب الحبر قال: والذي أنزل التوراة على موسى والإنجيل على عيسى والزبور على داود

DURR-FULL:v8p256/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan transmits a Prophetic scene in which idol-worshippers follow their objects, Jews and Christians are turned away, and Muslims remain to be tested before being permitted to prostrate.
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r9.anchor: عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يجمع الله الخلائق يوم القيامة ثم ينادي مناد

DURR-FULL:v8p257/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p257/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p257/r1.claim: In al-Ḥasan's report, Christians are also turned away, Muslims recognize God by a sign, and believers prostrate while hypocrites cannot; Ibn Masʿūd's Prophetic report adds that each person's light varies with deeds and may flicker at the feet.
DURR-FULL:v8p257/r1.anchor: لهم: لستم من موسى وليس موسى منكم فيصرف بهم ذات الشمال ثم يقال للنصارى: ما كنتم تعبدون

DURR-FULL:v8p257/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p257/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p257/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that people are gathered and shown what they worshipped; Muslims recognize their Lord by the sign of the unveiled ساق, believers prostrate, hypocrites cannot, and people receive light according to their deeds.
DURR-FULL:v8p257/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: يجمع الله الناس يوم القيامة وينزل الله في ظلل من الغمام

DURR-FULL:v8p259/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r1.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r1.claim: Kaʿb warns that Hell's blast makes every angel and prophet fall to their knees; even Abraham will plead for himself, and a person with the deeds of seventy prophets would still fear not escaping.
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r1.anchor: فقال كعب: يا أمير المؤمنين إن لجهنم زفرة ما من ملك ولا نبي إلا يخر لركبته

DURR-FULL:v8p259/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd recounts the Dajjāl's divisions and defeat by Jesus, Gog and Magog's devastation and destruction, the earth's cleansing, a cold wind killing survivors, then the Hour and resurrection; he cites 21:96.
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه ذكر عنده الدجال فقال: يفترق ثلاث فرق تتبعه فرقة تتبعه وفرقة تلحق بأرض آبائها

DURR-FULL:v8p259/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r3.claim: In the same report, Ibn Masʿūd cites the verse about God sending winds to raise clouds and revive dead land as an analogy for resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r3.anchor: ثم قرأ عبد الله (الله الذي يرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فسقناه إلى بلد ميت فأحيينا به الأرض بعد موتها

DURR-FULL:v8p259/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd cites the verse about Hell being displayed to unbelievers when describing the false worshippers' fate, and the command to halt them for questioning.
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه ذكر عنده الدجال فقال: يفترق ثلاث فرق تتبعه فرقة تتبعه

DURR-FULL:v8p259/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's report says Muslims affirm worshipping God alone; believers fall prostrate when the ساق is unveiled, but hypocrites' backs remain rigid, fulfilling the warning that they had been invited while safe.
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه ذكر عنده الدجال فقال: يفترق ثلاث فرق تتبعه فرقة تتبعه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās advises consulting Arabic poetry when Qurʾānic wording is unclear; the cited line about war standing on a ساق illustrates the idiom of severity.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r1.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس انه سئل عن قوله : يوم يكشف عن ساق قال : اذا خفى عليكم شيء من القران

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās calls it a day of distress and hardship.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هذا يوم كرب وشدة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās further glosses the phrase as a severe, appalling matter arising from the terror of Resurrection Day.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس يوم يكشف عن ساق قال : هو الامر الشديد المفظع من الهول يوم القيامة .

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s report says the Dajjāl draws three groups into following or fleeing; Jesus descends and kills him, then Gog and Magog spread corruption until God destroys them with a creature and cleanses the earth with rain.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود انه ذكر عنده الدجال فقال : يفترق ثلاث فرق تتبعه ،

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r5.claim: After a cold wind kills the remaining people and the Hour falls on the worst, the Trumpet kills creation except whom God wills; after the interval, bodies grow from water and people rise together for judgment.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود انه ذكر عنده الدجال فقال : يفترق ثلاث فرق تتبعه ،

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r6.claim: At judgment, people follow what they worshipped; Jews and Christians are led toward Hell, while Muslims profess God’s oneness and prostrate. Hypocrites cannot bend to prostrate though they had been called while safe.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود انه ذكر عنده الدجال فقال : يفترق ثلاث فرق تتبعه ،

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r7.claim: The bridge is laid over Hell, and people cross at speeds determined by their deeds, from a blink or lightning to crawling; the last is told that his deeds caused his delay.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r7.anchor: عن ابن مسعود انه ذكر عنده الدجال فقال : يفترق ثلاث فرق تتبعه ،

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r8.claim: Intercession begins with Gabriel, Abraham, and Moses or Jesus; Muhammad is fourth and holds the promised praised station. Everyone sees a Paradise and a Fire dwelling, making it the Day of Regret.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r8.anchor: عن ابن مسعود انه ذكر عنده الدجال فقال : يفترق ثلاث فرق تتبعه ،

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r9.claim: Angels, prophets, martyrs, the righteous, and believers intercede; by mercy God brings out everyone in Hell who has any good, and leaves no such person there.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r9.anchor: عن ابن مسعود انه ذكر عنده الدجال فقال : يفترق ثلاث فرق تتبعه ،

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r10.claim: The last people in Hell cannot recognize those seeking intercession; when they plead, God orders them away and silences them, then closes the Fire so no one remains there.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#4/r10.anchor: عن ابن مسعود انه ذكر عنده الدجال فقال : يفترق ثلاث فرق تتبعه ،

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r3.claim: One possible syntax attaches “the day” to the command to bring their alleged partners: let them bring them on Judgment Day, a transition to its terrors.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r3.anchor: يجوز أن يكون { يوم يكشف } متعلقا بقوله : { فليأتوا بشركائهم } ( القلم : 41 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r4.claim: Alternatively, it begins a new clause dependent on an omitted “remember,” recalling the horrors of that day.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون استئنافا متعلقا بمحذوف تقديره : اذكر يوم يكشف عن ساق ويدعون إلى السجود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r5.claim: On either syntactic reading, the day is the Day of Resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r5.anchor: وعلى كلا الوجهين في تعلق { يوم } فالمراد باليوم يوم القيامة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r6.claim: “Uncovering a shin” images severe distress: panicked people hurry and raise their clothes; crisis and war “uncovering a shin” are figurative, not literal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r6.anchor: والكشف عن ساق : مثل لشدة الحال وصعوبة الخطب والهول ، وأصله أن المرء إذا هلع أن يسرع في المشي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r7.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r7.claim: Anas reports that at Uḥud, ʿĀʾisha and Umm Sulaym carried water skins to the fighters, their raised clothes exposing their lower legs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r7.anchor: وفي حديث غزوة أحد قال أنس بن مالك : ( انهزم الناس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولقد رأيت عائشة وأم سليم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن قيس الرقيات
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r8.claim: Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt’s line shows war distracting a woman from concealing her legs, illustrating how crisis exposes the shin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p96/r8.anchor: قال عبد الله بن قيس الرقيات : كيف نومي على الفراش ولما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r1.claim: Ḥātim’s poem personifies war as raising its shin, poetic evidence for the idiom of crisis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r1.anchor: فتى الحرب عضت به لحرب الحرب عضها وإن شمرت عن ساقها الحرب شمرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r2.speaker: جد طرفة من الحماسة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r2.claim: A poem attributed to Ṭarafa’s grandfather likewise uses a woman uncovering her shin for an exposed crisis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r2.anchor: وقال جد طرفة من الحماسة : كشفت لهم عن ساقها وبدا من الشر البواح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads “the day it is uncovered” with feminine tāʾ and active voice, taking the subject as the distress or Resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس { يوم تكشف } بمثناة فوقية وبصيغة البناء للفاعل على تقدير تكشف الشدة عن ساقها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the uncovering of the shin as distress and hardship, the most severe hour of the Resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يكشف عن ساق : عن كرب وشدة ، وهي أشد ساعة في يوم القيامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r5.claim: ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and others report through ʿIkrima that Ibn ʿAbbās urged consulting Arab poetry for obscure Quranic expressions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r5.anchor: وروى عبد بن حميد وغيره عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس أنه سئل عن هذا ، فقال : ( إذا خفي عليكم شيء من القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r6.claim: Mujāhid glosses “uncovering a shin” as the severity of the affair.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد : { يكشف عن ساق } : شدة الأمر .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r7.claim: “They are summoned” does not refer to the earlier polytheists, since the following clause says they were called to prostrate in worldly life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r7.anchor: وجملة { ويدعون } ليس عائدا إلى المشركين مثل ضمير { إنا بلوناهم } ( القلم : 17 ) إذ لا يساعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r8.claim: The unstated group alludes to hypocrites raised among Muslims: the prostration test honors true believers and exposes hypocrites who cannot bow.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r8.anchor: فالوجه أن يكون عائدا إلى غير مذكور ، أي ويدعى مدعوون فيكون تعريضا بالمنافقين بأنهم يحشرون مع المسلمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
