IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r9.claim: Al-Qurṭubī quotes Ibn Masʿūd: sincere worshippers prostrate, while hypocrites cannot, as if their backs held skewers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r9.anchor: قال القرطبي عن قيس بن السكن عن عبد الله بن مسعود : فمن كان يعبد الله مخلصا يخر ساجدا له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r10.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r10.claim: In the vision and intercession report in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, the Prophet says sincere worshippers may prostrate, while show worshippers have rigid backs and fall backward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r10.anchor: وفي ( صحيح مسلم ) من حديث الرؤية وحديث الشفاعة عن أبي سعيد الخدري أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r1.speaker: فريق من المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r1.claim: Some exegetes say God uncovers a shin like a leg for people to see and classify this as ambiguous scripture.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r1.anchor: وقد اتبع فريق من المفسرين هذه الرواية وقالوا : يكشف الله عن ساقه ، أي عن مثل الرجل ليراها الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r2.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr reports that Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī transmitted a Prophetic interpretation of the shin as a great light at whose sight people prostrate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r2.anchor: روي عن أبي موسى الأشعري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله تعالى : { عن ساق }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says other reports on the phrase are weak and not worth recounting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r3.anchor: ورويت أخبار أخرى ضعيفة لا جدوى في ذكرها .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r4.claim: The summoned prostration is supplication and submission, sought as a way to escape the terrors of the gathering.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r4.anchor: و { السجود } الذي يدعون إليه : سجود الضراعة والخضوع لأجل الخلاص من أهوال الموقف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r5.claim: God removes their ability to prostrate so they learn that they have no hope of rescue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r5.anchor: وعدم استطاعتهم السجود لسلب الله منهم الاستطاعة على السجود ليعلموا أنهم لا رجاء لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r6.claim: The callers may be the angels assigned to the gathering, acting by God’s command, as in 54:6–8.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r6.anchor: والذي يدعوهم إلى السجود الملائكة الموكلون بالمحشر بأمر الله تعالى كقوله تعالى : { يوم يدعو الداعي إلى شيء نكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r7.claim: Alternatively, God inspires some people to call others to prostrate, as people call one another to seek intercession.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r7.anchor: أو يدعو بعضهم بعضا بإلهام من الله تعالى ، وهو نظير الدعوة إلى الشفاعة في الأثر المروي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r2.claim: Alternatively, ساق is an Arabic figure for hardship, as in ‘war rose on a leg’; the phrase means one calamity has overtaken another.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r2.anchor: وأنشد ابن عباس قول الراجز : صبرا عناق إنه لشرباق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p351#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p351#2/r9.speaker: بعض
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p351#2/r9.claim: Another view makes the challenge a summons to bring the partners on Resurrection Day, when the shin is uncovered.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p351#2/r9.anchor: وقيل هو استدعاء وتوقيف على أن يأتوا بهم يوم القيامة، يوم يكشف عن ساق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p351#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p351#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p351#2/r10.claim: Mujahid calls the first hour of Resurrection the most terrible part of that Day.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p351#2/r10.anchor: قال مجاهد: هي أول ساعة من يوم القيامة، وهي أفظعها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p351#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p351#2/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p351#2/r11.claim: A Prophetic report says worshippers follow what they worshipped, then the remaining people await their Lord, initially reject Him in another form, and recognize Him by a sign.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p351#2/r11.anchor: وتظاهر حديث من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أنه ينادي مناد يوم القيامة ليتبع كل أحد ما كان يعبد» ، قال: «فيتبع من كان يعبد الشمس الشمس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r1.claim: In the report’s continuation, people recognize God by a sign; after the unveiling, believers prostrate while hypocrites’ and disbelievers’ backs become rigid and they cannot prostrate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r1.anchor: فيكشف لهم عن ساق، فيقولون: نعم أنت ربنا، ويخرون للسجود فيسجد كل مؤمن وتصير أصلاب المنافقين والكفار كصياصي البقر عظما واحدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r2.claim: Although the report has variant additions and omissions, Ibn ʿAtiyya takes the unveiling of the shin as an expression of the Day’s terror and God’s overwhelming power, which all recognize as God’s alone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r2.anchor: هكذا هو الحديث وإن اختلفت منه ألفاظ بزيادة ونقصان، وعلى كل وجه فما ذكر فيه من كشف الساق وما في الآية أيضا من ذلك، فإنما هو عبارة عن شدة الهول وعظم القدرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r3.speaker: جد طرفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r3.claim: A war poem describes war as baring its shin, supporting the metaphor of severe struggle.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r3.anchor: ومن هذا المعنى قول الشاعر في صفة الحرب [جد طرفة] : مجزوء الكامل] كشفت لهم عن ساقها ... وبدا عن الشر البواح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r4.speaker: راجز وآخر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r4.claim: Two rajaz lines likewise portray a difficult year or conflict as baring its shin and requiring people to gird themselves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r4.anchor: ومنه قول الراجز: [الرجز] وشمرت عن ساقها فشدوا وقول الآخر: [الرجز] في سنة قد كشفت عن ساقها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r5.claim: The idiom originates in someone baring a shin when getting serious and exerting effort at a task.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r5.anchor: وأصل ذلك أنه من أراد الجد في أمر يحاوله فإنه يكشف عن ساقه تشميرا وجدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r6.speaker: دريد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r6.claim: Duraid’s praise poem about a warrior with half his shin exposed illustrates the idiom of serious exertion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r6.anchor: وقد مدح الشعراء بهذا المعنى فمنه قول دريد: [الطويل] كميش الإزار خارج نصف ساقه ... صبور على الضراء طلاع أنجد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r7.claim: The Prophet’s statement that a believer’s garment reaches mid-shin is linked to the same image of exertion and uncovering the leg.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r7.anchor: وعلى هذا من إرادة الجد والتشمير في طاعة الله تعالى، قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أزرة المؤمن إلى أنصاف ساقيه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r8.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r8.claim: Most readers use the passive form يكشف, with damma on ya.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r8.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس: «يكشف عن ساق» بضم الياء على بناء الفعل للمفعول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads يكشف actively, meaning God uncovers the shin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: «يكشف» بفتح الياء وكسر الشين على معنى يكشف الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas also reads تكشف with ta in the passive, making the Resurrection, severity, or present state the subject that is uncovered.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس: «تكشف» بضم التاء على معنى تكشف القيامة والشدة والحال الحاضرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r11.claim: A second reading from Ibn ʿAbbas has ta with fatḥa, so Resurrection itself is the revealer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس أيضا: «تكشف» بفتح التاء على أن القيامة هي الكاشفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r12.speaker: الأخفش وابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r12.claim: Al-Akhfash reports the nun reading نكشف, also transmitted from Ibn Masʿud, meaning we uncover.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r12.anchor: وحكى الأخفش عنه أنه قرأ: «نكشف» بالنون مفتوحة وكسر الشين، ورويت عن ابن مسعود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r13.claim: Because the afterlife is not an arena of deeds or legal obligation, the call is best understood as their seeing believers prostrate and wanting to follow, but being unable.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r13.anchor: وهذا يرده ما قد تقرر في الشرع من أن الآخرة ليست بدار عمل وأنها لا تكليف فيها، فإذا كان هذا فإنما الداعي ما يرونه من سجود المؤمنين فيريدون هم أن يسجدوا عند ذلك فلا يستطيعونه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r14.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r14.claim: Some scholars say they are called to prostrate as a form of rebuke.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r14.anchor: وقد ذهب بعض العلماء إلى أنهم يدعون إلى السجود على جهة التوبيخ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r15.claim: The inference that their present inability proves they previously had the ability is not necessary.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r15.anchor: وخرج بعض الناس من قوله: فلا يستطيعون أنهم كانوا يستطيعونه قبل ذلك، وذلك غير لازم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r16.speaker: الأشعري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r16.claim: Ashʿari doctrine holds that capacity exists together with performing the act, not before it; Ibn ʿAtiyya says that much suffices here.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r16.anchor: وعقيدة الأشعري: أن الاستطاعة إنما تكون مع التلبس بالفعل لما قبله، وهذا القدر كاف من هذه المسألة هاهنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r1.claim: This is the Day of Resurrection; the command to produce their partners is deferred until that day.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r2.claim: The majority read yukshafu with ḍamma on yāʾ and fatḥa on shīn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r2.anchor: قرأ الجمهور يكشف بضم الياء وفتح الشين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r3.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة، عاصم الجحدري، أبو الجوزاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r3.claim: They read yakshifu with fatḥa on yāʾ and kasra on shīn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة وعاصم الجحدري وأبو الجوزاء بفتح الياء وبكسر الشين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب، ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r4.claim: They read tukshafu with an open tāʾ and kasra on shīn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب وابن عباس تكشف بتاء مفتوحة وكسر الشين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود، أبو مجلز، ابن يعمر، الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r5.claim: They read nakshifu with an open nūn and kasra on shīn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبو مجلز وابن يعمر والضحاك نكشف بنون مفتوحة مع كسر الشين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the phrase as the onset of severe distress; Mujāhid and Qatāda hold the same view, and the source cites a war-onset idiom.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r6.anchor: وقد روى عكرمة عن ابن عباس يوم يكشف عن ساق قال يكشف عن شدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة، الفراء، أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba and the linguists say ساق is an idiom for hardship: a person rolls up his sleeves to face a difficult matter.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r7.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة وأصل هذا أن الرجل إذا وقع في أمر عظيم يحتاج إلى معاناته والجد فيه شمر عن ساقه فاستعيرت الساق في موضع الشدة هذا قول الفراء وأبي عبيدة واللغويين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r8.claim: A report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī says that God will uncover His ساق; Ibn al-Jawzī explains the attribution as an act and possession belonging to God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r8.anchor: فروي في الصحيحين من حديث أبي سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه يكشف عن ساقه وهذا إضافة إليه لأن الكل له وفعله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r9.speaker: أبو عمر الزاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r9.claim: An alternative takes ساق to mean the self, making the phrase mean that God becomes manifest to them; the source cites ʿAlī's line using ساق for self.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r9.anchor: وقال أبو عمر الزاهد يراد بها النفس ومنه قول علي رضي الله عنه أقاتلهم ولو تلفت ساقي أي نفسي فعلى هذا يكون المعنى يتجلى لهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r10.claim: The ones called to prostrate are the hypocrites; their backs are like iron spits, leaving them unable to bow.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r10.anchor: قوله تعالى ويدعون إلى السجود يعني المنافقين فلا يستطيعون كأن في ظهورهم سفافيد الحديد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r11.speaker: النقاش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r11.claim: This is not a legal demand that disabled people prostrate; it rebukes them for having abandoned prostration.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p340#3/r11.anchor: قال النقاش وليس ذلك بتكليف لهم أن يسجدوا وهم عجزة ولكنه توبيخ لهم بتركهم السجود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r1.claim: After mentioning Gardens of bliss for the God-fearing, Ibn Kathir explains when that promise occurs: on the Day of Resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r1.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى أن للمتقين عنده (1) جنات النعيم، بين متى ذلك كائن وواقع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r2.claim: The verse describes the Resurrection with its terrors, upheavals, trials, ordeals, and immense events.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r2.anchor: يعني: يوم القيامة وما يكون فيه من الأهوال والزلازل والبلاء والامتحان والأمور العظام.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي سعيد الخدري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r3.claim: Abu Saʿid reports the Prophet saying that the Lord uncovers His ساق; believers prostrate, while those who prostrated for show in worldly life cannot, their backs becoming rigid and flat. Ibn Kathir says the report is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and elsewhere.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "يكشف ربنا عن ساقه، فيسجد له كل مؤمن ومؤمنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the uncovering of the ساق as a day of distress and hardship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: هو يوم كرب وشدة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود أو ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud—or Ibn Abbas, with Ibn Jarir unsure—takes the phrase to mean a tremendous affair, supported by a poetic expression for war's intensity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود -أو: ابن عباس، الشك من ابن جرير-: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: عن أمر عظيم، كقول الشاعر: وقامت الحرب بنا عن ساق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r6.claim: Mujahid explains the phrase as the severity and intensity of the affair.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r6.anchor: وقال ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: شدة الأمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies it as the first hour of the Day of Resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هي أول (3) ساعة تكون في يوم القيامة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس عن علي بن أبي طلحة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas calls it the severe, terrifying event of the Resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r8.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} هو الأمر الشديد المفظع من الهول يوم القيامة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس عن العوفي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r9.claim: Al-ʿAwfi transmits Ibn Abbas's explanation that the affair is uncovered and deeds become manifest; other reports from Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak give the same account.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r9.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} يقول: حين يكشف الأمر وتبدو الأعمال.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي موسى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r10.claim: A report from the Prophet glosses the phrase as a great light before which people fall in prostration.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p198#3/r10.anchor: عن أبي بردة بن أبي موسى، عن أبيه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: {يوم يكشف عن ساق}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p199/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p199/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p199/r1.claim: Abu Yaʿla also transmits the Prophet's gloss of the ساق as a great light; the chain contains an unidentified man, and Ibn Kathir says God knows best.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p199/r1.anchor: ورواه أبو يعلى، عن القاسم بن يحيى، عن الوليد بن مسلم، به (4) وفيه رجل مبهم (5) والله أعلم.

JISHUMI:v10p7037/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7037/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7037/r4.claim: Sāq is the animal limb supporting its body and by extension a tree's trunk; a plant retaining a trunk through the seasons is a tree. The poet uses sāq for a limb.
JISHUMI:v10p7037/r4.anchor: والساق: عضو معروف للحيوان، سمي ساقا لقيام البدن عليه، ومنه: ساق الشجرة، وكل نبت له ساق يبقى صيفا وشتاء

JISHUMI:v10p7037/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7037/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7037/r5.claim: Kashf is removing a covering; “uncovering the shin” is an idiom for a severe crisis though war has no literal leg. Three poetic lines illustrate the idiom.
JISHUMI:v10p7037/r5.anchor: والكشف: إزالة الستر، ثم يستعمل كشف الساق في الأمور الشديدة، فيقال: قامت الحرب على ساق، وكشف الأمر عن ساق

JISHUMI:v10p7037/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7037/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7037/r6.claim: Most explain the idiom as depicting how a severe matter requires the leg to be bared; frequent use made it proverbial.
JISHUMI:v10p7037/r6.anchor: واختلفوا في تشبيه ذلك بكشف الساق، فالأكثر على أن معناه: أنه اشتد الأمر كما يشتد ما يحتاج إلى كشف الساق

JISHUMI:v10p7037/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7037/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7037/r7.claim: Abū Muslim traces the idiom to difficult extraction of a camel calf at birth; the helper was called a mudhammir, and sex and birth order were treated as omens. Al-Kumayt and another poet cite the custom.
JISHUMI:v10p7037/r7.anchor: وذكر أبو مسلم: أن أصله: استخراج ولد الناقة من خبائها عند الولادة، فيدخل الرجل يده ويخرجه

JISHUMI:v10p7041/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة والضحاك
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r7.claim: These authorities explain “uncovering the shin” as the terrible severity of that Day.
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r7.anchor: معناه: عن شدة من الأمر الفظيع من هول ذلك اليوم، عن ابن عباس، والحسن، ومجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير، وقتادة، والضحاك

JISHUMI:v10p7041/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r8.claim: Abū Muslim says it is the final day of worldly life and first day of the Hereafter, harsher than any day the servant has faced.
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r8.anchor: وقيل: هو عند الناس آخر أيام الدنيا، وأول يوم الآخرة لم يلق العبد يوما أشد منه، عن أبي مسلم.

JISHUMI:v10p7041/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r9.claim: Abū Muslim places the call to prayer at death, when angels appear and signs of the Hereafter become evident; they cannot respond.
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r9.anchor: قيل: يوم حضور الملائكة وظهور أعلام الآخرة وقت النزع، فيدعون إلى الصلاة (فلا يستطيعون)، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v10p7041/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r10.claim: Another view places this in the Hereafter: they are ordered to prostrate as a rebuke but cannot do so.
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r10.anchor: وقيل: هذا في الآخرة يؤمرون بالسجود تقريعا فلا يمكنهم

JISHUMI:v10p7041/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r11.claim: A further explanation says stiffness in their spines prevents them from prostrating.
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r11.anchor: وقيل: يحدث في أصلابهم صلابة تمنع من السجود

JISHUMI:v10p7042/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7042/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7042/r1.claim: The verse signifies the severity of the Resurrection's terrors; the call to prostrate is for rebuke, not worship.
JISHUMI:v10p7042/r1.anchor: ويدل قوله: (يكشف عن ساق) على شدة أهوال القيامة، وأنهم يدعون إلى السجود توبيخا لا تعبدا.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r1.claim: Uncovering the ساق and showing the ankles is a metaphor for a grave crisis; it originates in terror and defeat, when women hike their garments to flee.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r1.anchor: مثل في شدة الأمر وصعوبة الخطب ، وأصله في الروع والهزيمة وتشمير المخدرات عن سوقهن في الهرب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r2.claim: Hatim's line about war biting and baring its ساق witnesses the metaphor for an intensifying crisis.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r2.anchor: قال حاتم : أخو الحرب إن غضت به الحرب عضها … وإن شمرت عن ساقها الحرب شمرا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r3.claim: Ibn al-Ruqayyat's line about war displaying the ankles of a noble virgin witnesses the imagery of exposed ankles.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r3.anchor: وقال ابن الرقيات : تذهل الشيخ عن بنيه وتبدي … عن خدام العقيلة العذراء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r4.claim: The phrase means the crisis becomes severe; no literal uncovering or ساق occurs, just as ‘his hand is tied’ describes a miser without a real hand or bond.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r4.anchor: في معنى : يوم يشتد الأمر ويتفاقم ، ولا كشف ثم ولا ساق ، كماتقول للأقطع الشحيح : يده مغلولة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r5.claim: Those who make the phrase anthropomorphic do so, in the author's view, from narrow understanding and little knowledge of rhetoric.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r5.anchor: وأما من شبه فلضيق عطنه وقلة نظره في علم البيان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r6.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Masud says the Merciful uncovers His ساق, believers prostrate, and hypocrites' backs become rigid, like spits.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r6.anchor: حديث ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : ( 1220 ) ( يكشف الرحمن عن ساقه ؛ فأما المؤمنون فيخرون سجدا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r7.claim: The report's ساق means the severity and terror of God's affair on the Day of Resurrection, not a bodily limb.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r7.anchor: ومعناه : يشتد أمر الرحمن ويتفاقم هوله ، وهو الفزع الأكبر يوم القيامة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r8.claim: A literalist would need a definite form for a specific familiar ساق; the indefinite form signals an obscure, unprecedented terror, as in 54:6.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r8.anchor: للدلالة على أنه أمر مبهم في الشدة منكر خارج عن المألوف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r9.claim: Abu Ubayda says Muqatil ibn Sulayman anthropomorphized to embodiment, while Jahm ibn Safwan negated attributes to the point of disabling them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r9.anchor: وعن أبي عبيدة : خرج من خراسان رجلان ، أحدهما : شبه حتى مثل ، وهو مقاتل بن سليمان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r10.claim: Variants include نكشف with nūn and تكشف with tāʾ, active or passive, with the hour or crisis as subject; each means the crisis grows severe.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r10.anchor: وقرىء : ( يوم نكشف ) بالنون . وتكشف بالتاء على البناء للفاعل والمفعول جميعا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r11.claim: Another reading has tāʾ with ḍamma and kasra on ش; أكشف means to enter kashf, also said of a man whose upper lip turns up.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r11.anchor: وقرىء : ( تكشف ) بالتاء المضمومة كسر الشين ، من أكشف : إذا دخل في الكشف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r12.claim: The time adverb is governed by فليأتوا, by an implicit اذكر, or by an omitted clause suppressed to heighten the threat.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r12.anchor: وناصب الظرف : فليأتوا . أو إضمار ( اذكر ) أو يوم يكشف عن ساق كان كيت وكيت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r1.claim: In most sciences, scholars’ and craftspeople’s ranks are close, with only small differences in advancement.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r1.anchor: متن كل علم وعمود كل صناعة طبقات العلماء فيه متدانية وأقدام الصناع فيه متقاربة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r2.claim: The greatest disparities arise in subtle insights, fine meanings, and hidden secrets that only the rarest specialists can uncover.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r2.anchor: ما في العلوم والصناعات من محاسن النكت والفقر ومن لطائف معان يدق فيها مباحث للفكر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r3.claim: Tafsīr is the richest and most demanding science because its fine points overwhelm minds and its hidden meanings are difficult to reach; al-Jāḥiẓ makes this point in Naẓm al-Qurʾān.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r3.anchor: علم التفسير الذي لا يتم لتعاطيه وإجالة النظر فيه كل ذي علم كما ذكر الجاحظ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r4.claim: Expertise in law, theology, reports, preaching, grammar, or lexicon alone does not qualify one to interpret; the interpreter must excel in Qurʾānic semantics and eloquence and master other fields through study and review.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r4.anchor: لا يتصدى منهم أحد لسلوك تلك الطرائق ولا يغوص على شيء من تلك الحقائق الا رجل قد برع في علمين مختصين بالقرآن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r5.claim: The qualified interpreter must have a precise, alert, flexible mind, command of prose and verse styles, and practice arranging and composing words.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p42/r5.anchor: مسترسل الطبيعة منقادها مشتعل القريحة وقادها يقظان النفس دراكا للمحة وإن لطف شأنها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r1.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r1.claim: One explanation is that this is the ساق of the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r1.anchor: أحدها : عن ساق الآخرة , قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r2.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r2.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas glosses ساق as covering, citing a rajaz line about a year exposing its ساق.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r2.anchor: الثاني : الساق الغطاء , قاله الربيع بن أنس , ومنه قول الراجز :

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the phrase as an idiom for distress and hardship, supported by a poem about hardship appearing openly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r3.anchor: الثالث : أنه الكرب والشدة , قاله ابن عباس , ومنه قول الشاعر :

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r4.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says it marks the arrival of the afterlife and the end of worldly life, the first of the hardships; a war poem illustrates the idiom.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r4.anchor: الرابع : هو إقبال الآخرة وذهاب الدنيا , قال الضحاك : لأنه أول الشدائد , كما قال الراجز :

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r5.claim: Reports that God unveils His ساق cannot be literal: God is beyond parts and limbs and being uncovered or covered; the phrase may mean a great divine matter or God's light.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r5.anchor: فإن الله تعالى منزه عن التبعيض والأعضاء وأن ينكشف أو يتغطى , ومعناه أنه يكشف عن العظيم من أمره , وقيل يكشف عن نوره .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r6.claim: The day may refer to old age and incapacity for deeds.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r6.anchor: أحدها : أنه يوم الكبر والهرم والعجز عن العمل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r7.claim: It may instead be the day of death and direct witnessing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r7.anchor: الثاني : أنه يوم حضور المنية والمعاينة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r8.claim: A third view identifies it as the Day of Resurrection.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r9.claim: If the day is the Resurrection, the call to prostrate is a binding command.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r9.anchor: فمن قال في هذا اليوم إنه يوم القيامة جعل الأمر بهذا السجود على وجه التكليف .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r10.claim: If the day is in worldly life, one view is that the call to prostrate is a binding command.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r10.anchor: ومن جعله في الدنيا فلهم في الأمر بهذا السجود قولان : أحدهما : أنه تكليف .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r11.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r11.claim: Another worldly-life reading makes the call a rebuke for their inability; Ibn Bahr says it came while they could prostrate, and they cannot later make up what they neglected.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p70/r11.anchor: الثاني : تندم وتوبيخ للعجز عنه , وكان ابن بحر يذهب إلى أن هذا الدعاء إلى السجود إنما كان في وقت الاستطاعة ,

MUJAHID:v2p689#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p689#2/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
MUJAHID:v2p689#2/r1.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports the Prophet saying that those who prostrated willingly in life will be allowed to prostrate, while those who did so from fear or ostentation will be unable, their backs made rigid so they fall on them.
MUJAHID:v2p689#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول يكشف ربنا عز وجل عن ساقه

MUQATIL:68:42-43/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r1.claim: The uncovering refers to the severity of the afterlife, glossed through the earth shining with its Lord’s light.
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r1.anchor: يعني قوله: { وأشرقت الأرض بنور ربها } يعني عن شدة الآخرة

MUQATIL:68:42-43/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r2.speaker: عبدالله بن مسعود
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says the light of God's right leg illuminates the earth, explaining the earth shining with its Lord’s light.
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: قال ابن مسعود في قوله: { يوم يكشف عن ساق } يعني فيضىء نور ساقه الأرض

MUQATIL:68:42-43/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the phrase as the distress of the afterlife, like the idiom that war has arisen on a ساق; it is the uncovering of its terrors.
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل: وقال ابن عباس، رضي الله عنه، في قوله { يوم يكشف عن ساق } يعني عند شدة الآخرة

MUQATIL:68:42-43/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r4.claim: The unbelievers’ backs freeze into a single bone, like cattle horns, because they did not prostrate in earthly life.
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r4.anchor: تجمد أصلاب الكفار فتكون كالصياصى عظما واحدا مثل صياصى البقر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r1.claim: The temporal phrase attaches to an omitted “فليأتوا” or “اذكر”.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r1.anchor: ناسب الظرف فليأتوا أو اذكر مضمرا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r2.speaker: الجمهور
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r2.claim: The majority take “uncovering the shin” as an idiom for the severity and hardship of the affair; no literal shin is uncovered.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r2.anchor: والجمهور على أن الكشف عن الساق عبارة عن شدة الامر وصعوبة الخطب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r3.claim: The idiom evokes people baring their shins in hardship, as “his hand is shackled” can figuratively mean stinginess without any actual shackle.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r3.anchor: ولا كشف ثمة ولا ساق ولكن كنى به عن الشدة لانهم إذا ابتلوا بشدة كشفوا عن الساق

NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r4.speaker: المشبهة
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r4.claim: Al-Nasafi rejects the anthropomorphists' literal reading as narrow-minded and deficient in rhetorical understanding; it would require a definite, familiar shin.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r4.anchor: وأما من شبه فلضيق عطنه وقلة نظر في علم البيان ولو كان الامر كما زعم المشبهة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r5.claim: The disbelievers are called to prostrate as a rebuke for abandoning prostration in worldly life, not as a legal obligation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r5.anchor: لا نكليفا ولكن توبيخا على تركهم السجود في الدنيا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r6.claim: They cannot prostrate because their backs become like cattle's stiff legs and will not bend for bowing or rising.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p271#10/r6.anchor: ذلك لأن ظهورهم تصير كصيا البقر لا تنثني عند الخفض والرفع

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r1.claim: Yawm may be governed by fa-l-ya'tū, in which case the pause at ṣādiqīn is not taken, or by an implied udhkur, allowing the pause.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون العامل في «يوم» «فليأتوا» أي فليأتوا بشركائهم يوم يكشف عن ساق

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r2.claim: A reading has the first-person plural form yawma nakshifu, 'the day We uncover.'

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reads yawma takshifu with an explicit feminine subject, meaning hardship or Resurrection bares its shin, as in the Arabic idiom that war bares its shin.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r3.anchor: «وقرأ» ابن عباس «يوم تكشف عن ساق» بتاء مسمى الفاعل

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r4.claim: Qurtubi cites several poems using war's uncovering of its shin to establish the idiom for the onset of hardship.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r4.anchor: فتى الحرب إن عضت به الحرب عضها وإن شمرت عن ساقها الحرب شمرا

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، أبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and Abu al-Aliya also read takshifu with a feminine verb lacking an expressed subject; it returns to the sense that Resurrection reveals hardship.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا والحسن وأبي العالية «تكشف» بتاء غير مسمى الفاعل. وهذه القراءة راجعة إلى معنى «يكشف»

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r6.claim: Another reading has feminine takshifu with a damma on tāʾ and kasra on shīn, from akshafa, meaning to enter exposure; akshafa can describe an upper lip turned up.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r6.anchor: وقرىء «يوم تكشف» بالتاء المضمومة وكسر الشين من أكشف إذا دخل في الكشف.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as distress and hardship.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r7.anchor: وذكر ابن المبارك قال: أخبرنا أسامة بن زيد عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى: { يوم يكشف عن ساق } قال: عن كرب وشدة.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r8.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r8.claim: Mujahid glosses it as the severity and seriousness of the affair, and reports Ibn Abbas's view that it is the hardest hour of Judgment Day.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r8.anchor: أخبرنا ابن جريج عن مجاهد قال: شدة الأمر وجده. وقال مجاهد: قال ابن عباس هي أشد ساعة في يوم القيامة.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r9.claim: Abu Ubayda says Arabs use 'the matter uncovered its shin' when war or a situation intensifies; the expression comes from one who rolls up his shin to exert himself.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r9.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: إذا اشتد الحرب والأمر قيل: كشف الأمر عن ساقه. والأصل فيه أن من وقع في شيء يحتاج فيه إلى الجد شمر عن ساقه

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r10.claim: Another explanation takes sāq as a thing's sustaining root, like a tree's or a person's leg: the affair's root is exposed and realities become clear.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r10.anchor: وقيل: ساق الشيء أصله الذي به قوامه كساق الشجرة وساق الإنسان. أي يوم يكشف عن أصل الأمر فتظهر حقائق الأمور وأصلها.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r11.claim: Other reported explanations identify the revealed shin as the shin of Hell or the shin of the Throne.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r11.anchor: وقيل: يكشف عن ساق جهنم. وقيل: عن ساق العرش.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r12.claim: One explanation describes a dying, weakened patient uncovering his shin; the caller summons him to prayer, but he cannot rise and go out.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r12.anchor: وقيل: يريد وقت اقتراب الأجل وضعف البدن أي يكشف المريض عن ساقه ليبصر ضعفه، ويدعوه المؤذن إلى الصلاة فلا يمكنه أن يقوم ويخرج.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r13.claim: Qurtubi rejects interpreting the phrase as a bodily limb of God, since God transcends body parts and being uncovered or covered; it means disclosure of a great matter.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r13.anchor: فأما ما روي أن الله يكشف عن ساقه فإنه عز وجل يتعالى عن الأعضاء والتبعيض وأن يكشف ويتغطى. ومعناه أن يكشف عن العظيم من أمره.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r14.claim: Another interpretation says the phrase means that God's light is revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r14.anchor: وقيل: يكشف عن نوره عز وجل.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r15.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r15.claim: Abu Musa transmits from the Prophet that a great light is unveiled and people fall prostrate; Qurtubi gives no grading here.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r15.anchor: وروى أبو موسى: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله تعالى: «عن ساق» قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#2/r1.claim: Abu Musa reports that on Judgment Day each people follows what it worshipped; the monotheists await their Lord, recognize Him despite not having seen Him, and prostrate when the veil is lifted, while some cannot. The account ends with each being replaced by a Jew or Christian in Hell; no grading is stated.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو الليث السمرقندي في تفسيره: حدثنا الخليل بن أحمد قال حدثنا ابن منيع قال حدثنا هدبة قال حدثنا حماد بن سلمة عن علي بن زيد عن عمارة القرشي عن أبي بردة عن أبي موسى قال حدثني أبي قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r1.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r1.claim: Abu Bardah swore three times that his father had told him the Abu Musa report; Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said he had heard no report about monotheists he liked more.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r1.anchor: قال أبو بردة: فحدثت بهذا الحديث عمر بن عبد العزيز فقال: الله الذي لا إله إلا هو لقد حدثك أبوك بهذا الحديث؟

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r2.claim: Qays ibn al-Sakan reports Ibn Masud's account: after a forty-year standing and a call about divine justice, groups follow their objects of worship into Hell; Muslims and hypocrites await God, but sincere worshippers prostrate when He is revealed and hypocrites cannot.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r2.anchor: وقال قيس بن السكن: حدث عبد الله بن مسعود عند عمر بن الخطاب فقال:

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r3.claim: Qurtubi says the meaning of the Abu Musa and Ibn Masud accounts is established in Sahih Muslim through Abu Said al-Khudri and others.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r3.anchor: قلت: معنى حديث أبي موسى وابن مسعود ثابت في صحيح مسلم من حديث أبي سعيد الخدري وغيره.
